Teach us to ask, to search and to knock with the trust of children, and to give to others the goodness we long to receive from you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: At Mass we ask, and the Father gives us not a stone but the true Bread from heaven: his own Son.

2027-02-19.title: Friday of the First Week of Lent
readings: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, and not rather that they should turn and live?
If you, O Lord, mark iniquities, Lord, who can stand?
Go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister
2027-02-19.alt: Lenten weekday, First Week of Lent. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Friday of abstinence: the Fridays of Lent are days of abstinence from meat.
2027-02-19.verse: leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
theo: The exiles in Babylon had a proverb: “The parents have eaten sour grapes, and the children's teeth are set on edge.” We are paying for our ancestors' sins, they said; nothing we do can change our fate. Ezekiel answers with God's own word: every person stands before God in his own present choice. “If the wicked turn away from all their sins that they have committed… they shall surely live; they shall not die. None of the transgressions that they have committed shall be remembered against them.” And then the heart of the chapter: “Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?” The warning cuts the other way too: the righteous who turn to evil cannot hide behind their past goodness. Neither our past sins nor our past virtues decide our future; what matters is the turning of the heart now. That is why Lent is always hopeful: it is never too late to turn and live. The Psalm prays it from the depths: “If you, O LORD, should mark iniquities, Lord, who could stand? But there is forgiveness with you.”

Jesus asks for a righteousness that “exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees”. Not a longer list of rules, but a law written deeper in the heart. “You have heard that it was said… ‘You shall not murder’… But I say to you that if you are angry with a brother or sister, you will be liable to judgment.” Murder begins long before the knife, in contempt, insult and anger nursed in secret. Then Jesus says something astonishing about worship: “So when you are offering your gift at the altar, if you remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.” God would rather wait for our gift than receive it from a divided heart. On this Lenten Friday, when we abstain from meat, the better fast is to abstain from anger and to go first to the one we have hurt.
outline: Ask: is anyone ever too far gone to change?
God takes no pleasure in death.
Anger is the root of murder.
“First be reconciled to your brother or sister.”
live: Go first (Matthew 5:24)
Take the first step today towards someone who has something against you.
Abstain from anger
Keep today's abstinence also by refusing every insult and harsh word.
2027-02-19.prayer: Lord God, you take no pleasure in the death of sinners but desire that they turn and live. Turn our hearts to you this Lent. Uproot from us the anger that kills love, and give us courage to go first to those we have hurt, so that our gifts at the altar may be pleasing to you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Before Communion we exchange the sign of peace. Jesus asks that our peace be real: reconciled with one another, we come to the altar to offer our gift.

2027-02-20.title: Saturday of the First Week of Lent
readings: You shall be a people holy to the Lord your God
Blessed are they who follow the law of the Lord!
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect
2027-02-20.alt: Lenten weekday, First Week of Lent. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-20.verse: But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
theo: Moses, at the end of his long journey with Israel, describes the covenant as a solemn exchange of promises made “this very day”. “Today you have obtained the LORD's agreement: to be your God; and for you to walk in his ways… Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people.” It sounds almost like a marriage vow. God binds himself to Israel, and Israel binds itself to God. The word “treasured” translates the Hebrew segullah, the private treasure a king keeps for himself apart from the state treasury. Israel is God's personal treasure, set “high above all nations”, not for pride but to be “a people holy to the LORD your God”. Every Christian has made this same exchange of promises at baptism, and every Mass renews it. In Lent we are invited to say again, “today”, that we belong to him and will walk in his ways.

Jesus now shows how far the ways of God reach. “You have heard that it was said, ‘You shall love your neighbor and hate your enemy.’ But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good, and sends rain on the righteous and on the unrighteous.” The sun does not choose whom to warm. If we love only those who love us, Jesus says, we are doing nothing more than tax collectors and pagans. Then comes the summit of the Sermon: “Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.” This perfection is not flawlessness but completeness of love: a love that, like the Father's, excludes no one. It is impossible on our own; it is the work of grace in God's treasured people. As the first week of Lent ends, we bring to God the one person we find hardest to love, and we pray for them by name.
outline: Ask: whom do you find hardest to pray for?
Like the sun on the evil and the good.
“Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
live: Pray by name (Matthew 5:44)
Pray today for someone who has wronged you, by name, asking God to bless them.
Greet the one you avoid (Matthew 5:47)
Greet warmly someone you usually ignore.
2027-02-20.prayer: Father in heaven, you make your sun rise on the evil and on the good, and you have chosen us as your treasured people. Renew in us today the promises of our baptism. Give us a heart like yours, that we may love our enemies, pray for those who persecute us, and grow towards the perfection of your love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: Every Mass renews the covenant: in the Blood of the new and eternal covenant, God says again “you are mine”, and we answer “Amen”. Christ, who prayed for his persecutors from the cross, teaches us to pray for ours.

2027-02-22.title: The Chair of St Peter, Apostle
readings: As an elder myself, I exhort the elders: tend the flock of God
The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want
You are Peter, and to you I will give the keys of the kingdom of heaven
2027-02-22.alt: Feast. The readings of Monday of the Second Week of Lent give way to those of the feast. The Gloria is said; the Gospel acclamation is sung without Alleluia, as throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: white.
2027-02-22.verse: And I tell you, you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.
theo: In the second week of Lent the Church pauses for a feast of white: the Chair of St Peter. A chair seems a strange thing to celebrate. But in the ancient world the cathedra was the seat from which a teacher taught and a bishop presided; Jesus himself speaks of the scribes who “sit on Moses' seat” (Matthew 23:2). Since at least the fourth century the Church of Rome has kept this day in honour of Peter's chair, that is, of the mission Christ gave him to teach, to guide and to hold the Church together in one faith. We do not honour a piece of wood. We honour the Lord, who chose a fisherman and made him a rock, and who still keeps his Church united around Peter's successor.

The Gospel takes us to Caesarea Philippi, far in the north, where a great rock face rose above a shrine to pagan gods. There Jesus asks two questions. First: “Who do people say that the Son of Man is?” The answers are generous but not enough: John the Baptist, Elijah, Jeremiah, a prophet. Then the question that no one can answer for us: “But who do you say that I am?” Simon speaks for all: “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.” Jesus tells him that this faith is a gift: “flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father in heaven.” Then he gives Simon a new name. “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it.” In Aramaic the name and the rock are the same word, Kepha. He gives him the keys of the kingdom, the sign of a steward over the king's house, as Isaiah once said of Eliakim: “he shall open, and no one shall shut.” And he gives the power to bind and to loose.

Peter did not become a rock by his own strength. The same chapter tells how he tried to turn Jesus away from the cross and heard the words “Get behind me, Satan!” Later he denied his Master three times. His firmness comes from the prayer of Jesus: “I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.” That is why the first reading sounds so humble. The old Apostle writes as “an elder myself and a witness of the sufferings of Christ,” and asks the shepherds to tend the flock “not under compulsion but willingly,” not lording it over others but being examples, until “the chief shepherd appears.” The Psalm names that chief Shepherd: “The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want.” In Lent this feast reminds us that conversion is never private. We return to God within the one flock, under the one Shepherd, held together by the faith Peter confessed.
conn: Caesarea Philippi.
A town at the foot of Mount Hermon, near a cave and rock face where Pan was worshipped. Against that rock of false gods Jesus names the true rock.
Kepha.
Jesus spoke Aramaic; Kepha means rock. Greek turned it into Petros. Paul often calls him Cephas (Galatians 2:9; 1 Corinthians 15:5).
The keys.
Isaiah 22:22 describes the steward of the royal house receiving the key of the house of David. The keys mean authority given in trust, on behalf of the king.
Bind and loose.

Rabbinic terms for deciding what is permitted and forbidden, and for admitting to or excluding from the community. Christ gives this authority to Peter, and later to the apostles together (Matthew 18:18).
The chair.

Cathedra means seat of teaching; a cathedral is the church where the bishop's chair stands. In St Peter's Basilica, Bernini's bronze Chair (1666) encloses an ancient wooden chair venerated as a relic.
An ancient feast.

A Roman list of feasts from the year 354 already marks 22 February for Peter's chair. The day was also linked with the old Roman custom of honouring the dead of one's family: the Church honoured her father in the faith.
altar: At every Mass the Pope is named in the Eucharistic Prayer, together with our bishop. We are praying in communion with Peter.
The Shepherd who spreads a table for us (Psalm 23:5) feeds his flock with his own Body, and the unity of the Church is both shown and made at the altar.
outline: Ask: who taught you the faith, and how did they hold you steady?
Point 1 · Who do you say that I am?
The question no one can answer for us.
A rock made by grace, not by strength.
Authority given in trust, for service.
A fisherman's chair at the heart of the Church.
“You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
live: Answer the question (Matthew 16:15)
Today, in your own words, tell Jesus who he is for you.
Pray for the Pope
Pray the Our Father and a Hail Mary for the Holy Father, that his faith may not fail.
Pray for your bishop and priests
Name your bishop and parish priest in prayer, and thank them for one thing.
Build unity
Where there is division in your family or parish, take one step toward peace this week.
fathers: St Cyprian of Carthage (in substance)
The Lord built the Church upon one, so that unity might be shown from its source. Whoever abandons the chair of Peter on which the Church is founded cannot be sure he is in the Church.
St Leo the Great (in substance)
The firmness that Peter received from Christ the Rock passes on to his heirs. Wherever his successor teaches in faith, Peter is still at work, strengthening his brothers.
St Ambrose (in substance)
Where Peter is, there is the Church; and where the Church is, there is not death but life eternal.
magis: Catechism 552–553
Peter's confession, the rock and the keys: the power to bind and loose.
Catechism 880–882
The college of bishops and its head, the Roman Pontiff, the perpetual source of unity.
Catechism 936–937
The Pope, Bishop of Rome and successor of Peter.
Lumen Gentium 18, 22
Vatican II: Peter's successor as the visible foundation of the unity of faith and communion.
Catechism 754, 1548–1551
Christ the Good Shepherd and the ministry of shepherds in his Church.
saints: St Peter the Apostle

Fisherman of Bethsaida and Capernaum, called by Jesus, named Rock, first among the Twelve. He led the Church in Jerusalem and later in Rome, where he was crucified under Nero about AD 64 and buried on the Vatican Hill.
This week
23 Feb: St Polycarp (commemoration). 24–26 Feb: Lenten weekdays. 27 Feb: St Gregory of Narek (commemoration). 28 Feb: Third Sunday of Lent; First Scrutiny of the elect.
2027-02-22.prayer: Grant, we pray, almighty God, that no tempests may disturb us, for you have set us fast on the rock of the Apostle Peter's confession of faith. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, your Son, who lives and reigns with you in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, for ever and ever. Amen. Let us also pray: Lord Jesus, Son of the living God, you built your Church on Peter. Keep our Holy Father strong in faith and gentle in love; bless our bishop and priests; and make us one flock, faithful to you through this Lent and always. Amen.

2027-02-23.title: Tuesday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Learn to do good. Though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow
To the upright I will show the saving power of God
They do not practise what they teach. The greatest among you will be your servant
2027-02-23.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St Polycarp, bishop and martyr (its collect may be used).
2027-02-23.verse: The greatest among you will be your servant. All who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted.
theo: Isaiah speaks to the rulers of Jerusalem as if they were the rulers of Sodom. Their temple is full of sacrifices, but their hands are full of blood. God does not want more ritual; he wants a changed life: “Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean; remove the evil of your doings from before my eyes; cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow.” Then comes one of the most tender invitations in the Bible: “Come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow.” God reasons with his people like a father with a son who has gone wrong. The Psalm says the same: God does not need our bulls and goats; what honours him is a thankful heart and a straight road: “to those who go the right way I will show the salvation of God.”

In the Gospel Jesus warns against a religion of display. The scribes and Pharisees “sit on Moses' seat”, and what they teach from the law should be done, “but do not do as they do, for they do not practice what they teach.” They tie heavy burdens on others and will not lift a finger; they love the best seats and the greetings in the market and the title “rabbi”. Jesus turns this upside down: you have one teacher, one Father, one instructor, the Messiah, and you are all brothers and sisters. “The greatest among you will be your servant.” Lent is a time to check whether our faith is lived or only displayed. Today we remember St Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna, a disciple of St John the Apostle, who served his people for decades and was burned at the stake about the year 155, at the age of eighty-six. When the proconsul told him to curse Christ, he answered (in substance): for eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong; how can I blaspheme my King who saved me? He practised what he taught, to the end.
outline: Ask: whom do you trust more, someone who talks well or someone who lives well?
God's invitation to reason and be washed.
Jesus warns against a religion of display.
“The greatest among you will be your servant.”
live: Learn to do good (Isaiah 1:17)
Do one concrete act of justice or help for a widow, an orphan or someone who is overlooked.
Practise what you teach
Choose one thing you often tell others to do, and do it yourself today.
2027-02-23.prayer: Merciful Father, you call us to wash ourselves and learn to do good. Make our sins white as snow, free us from the love of honour, and make us servants of one another. Through the prayers of St Polycarp, faithful bishop and martyr, keep us loyal to Christ our King to the end. Amen.
altar: Christ, the one Teacher, became the servant of all and gives himself at the altar. In him our worship and our life become one offering.

2027-02-24.title: Wednesday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Come, let us make plots against Jeremiah
Save me, O Lord, in your steadfast love
They will condemn him to death
2027-02-24.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-24.verse: just as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.”
theo: Jeremiah has spoken God's word faithfully, and now the people plot against him. They say: let us bring charges against him and not heed any of his words. The prophet turns to God in pain: “Is evil a recompense for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them, to turn away your wrath from them.” He had prayed for the very people who now want him dead. Jeremiah is a figure of Christ, the innocent one who intercedes for those who reject him. The Psalm puts the words of trust on our lips that Jesus himself prayed on the cross: “Into your hand I commit my spirit; you have redeemed me, O LORD, faithful God.” And again: “My times are in your hand.”

In the Gospel Jesus, going up to Jerusalem, tells the Twelve for the third time what awaits him: he will be handed over, condemned, mocked, flogged and crucified, “and on the third day he will be raised.” At that very moment the mother of James and John kneels before him and asks for the best places in his kingdom. Jesus answers gently: “You do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink?” They say, “We are able,” not knowing that the cup is suffering. And the other ten are angry, perhaps because they wanted the same places. So Jesus teaches them all: among the nations rulers lord it over others, “It will not be so among you; but whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant.” Then he gives the reason, the heart of the whole Gospel: “the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many.” In Lent we follow him up to Jerusalem. The question is not which seat we will have, but whether we will drink his cup with him.
outline: Ask: if you could ask Jesus for one honour, what would it be?
Jeremiah, the prophet who prayed for his enemies.
Point 2 · Can you drink the cup?
Point 3 · Not to be served but to serve
“The Son of Man came not to be served but to serve.”
live: Serve, do not seek to be served (Matthew 20:28)
Take the lowest task at home or at work today without comment.
Pray for those who hurt you
Like Jeremiah, speak good of someone before God who has spoken ill of you.
2027-02-24.prayer: Lord Jesus, you went up to Jerusalem to give your life as a ransom for many. Free us from the desire for the first places, teach us to drink your cup with trust, and make us servants of all. Into your hands we commit our spirit. Amen.
altar: The cup that Jesus asked the disciples to drink is the cup he offers us at every Mass: the cup of his Blood, poured out for many. To receive it is to share his self-giving love.

2027-02-25.title: Thursday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Cursed is the one who trusts in mortals; blessed is the one who trusts in the Lord
Happy are they who hope in the Lord
You received your good things, and Lazarus evil things; now he is comforted here, and you are in agony
2027-02-25.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet.
2027-02-25.verse: There was a rich man who was dressed in purple and fine linen and who feasted sumptuously every day. And at his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores,
theo: Jeremiah sets two pictures side by side. The one who trusts in mere mortals and turns his heart from the LORD “shall be like a shrub in the desert,” living in parched places where nothing good comes. But “Blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD. They shall be like a tree planted by water, sending out its roots by the stream. It shall not fear when heat comes, and its leaves shall stay green; in the year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.” In Kerala we know such trees by the backwaters: in the hottest May they stay green because their roots reach the water. Then Jeremiah looks inside: the human heart is devious and hard to understand, but “I the LORD test the mind and search the heart, to give to all according to their ways.” Where are the roots of my heart? In money, in people's opinion, in my own strength, or in God?

Jesus answers with a story. A rich man, dressed in purple and fine linen, feasts every day. At his gate lies a poor man, covered with sores, longing for the scraps from the table; only the dogs come to him. The rich man is never said to be cruel. He simply does not see. The poor man has a name, Lazarus, which means God helps; the rich man has none. Both die. Lazarus is carried by the angels to Abraham's side; the rich man finds himself in torment and begs for a drop of water. Abraham reminds him: you received your good things in your lifetime; and between us and you a great chasm has been fixed. The chasm in eternity is the gate he never crossed in time. Then the rich man begs for his five brothers, and Abraham replies: “If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead.” Lent asks us to open our eyes to the Lazarus at our gate, while there is still time, and to listen to the One who has indeed risen from the dead.
outline: Ask: whom do you pass every day without really seeing?
Trust in mortals or trust in the Lord.
Point 2 · The man at the gate
“Blessed are those who trust in the LORD.”
live: Look at the gate (Luke 16:20)
Notice one poor or suffering person near you today, learn their name and do something for them.
Check your roots (Jeremiah 17:7)
Ask in prayer: what am I really trusting in? Hand it to God.
2027-02-25.prayer: Lord God, you search the heart and know us. Root us in trust in you like a tree beside the water, open our eyes to the Lazarus at our gate, and make us listen to your word while there is time. Through Christ our Lord, who rose from the dead. Amen.
altar: At the altar the Lord sets a table for all. The Eucharist sends us out to see Christ in the poor, as the Church Fathers taught: whoever honours the Body of Christ on the altar must honour it in the poor.

2027-02-26.title: Friday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: Here comes this dreamer. Come now, let us kill him
Remember the marvels the Lord has done
This is the heir; come, let us kill him
2027-02-26.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Friday of Lent: abstinence from meat (or another penance as your bishops' conference determines). Many parishes pray the Way of the Cross today.
2027-02-26.verse: Jesus said to them, “Have you never read in the scriptures: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was the Lord's doing, and it is amazing in our eyes’?
theo: On the Fridays of Lent the Church sets before us the mystery of the beloved son who is rejected. Joseph is his father's favourite, “the son of his old age,” and Jacob makes him a long robe with sleeves. His brothers hate him and “could not speak peaceably to him.” When Jacob sends him to see how they are, they see him coming from far off and say: “Here comes this dreamer. Come now, let us kill him and throw him into one of the pits.” Reuben saves his life; Judah suggests a profit instead: they sell him to traders “for twenty pieces of silver,” and he is taken down to Egypt. Envy has done its work. But the Psalm sings what the brothers could not see: God “had sent a man ahead of them, Joseph, who was sold as a slave.” The one they threw into the pit would one day feed them in a famine and forgive them. Years later Joseph would say: “Even though you intended to do harm to me, God intended it for good.”

In the Gospel Jesus tells the story of a vineyard owner who plants, fences, builds a tower and leases it to tenants. At harvest he sends servants for his share; the tenants beat one, kill another, stone another. Last of all he sends his son: “They will respect my son.” But the tenants say: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him and get his inheritance.” They throw him out of the vineyard and kill him. The chief priests and Pharisees realise he is speaking about them. Jesus is telling his own story, a few days before it happens: he will be sold for silver like Joseph, taken outside the city and killed. And yet, “The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was the Lord's doing.” God turns the worst that sin can do into the foundation of our salvation. On this Lenten Friday we ask: do I welcome the Son, or do I want the vineyard for myself? And what fruit am I giving to the Lord of the vineyard?
outline: Ask: has envy ever pushed you to do or say something you regretted?
Joseph, envy and twenty pieces of silver.
The parable that tells the Passion in advance.
“The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone.”
live: Uproot envy (Genesis 37:4)
Name one person you envy, and pray for their good today.
Bear fruit for the Lord (Matthew 21:43)
Choose one fruit God is asking of you this Lent, and give it today.
2027-02-26.prayer: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, you were sold and thrown out and killed, yet you became the cornerstone of our salvation. Free us from envy and greed, make us fruitful tenants of your vineyard, and turn all our sufferings to good. Amen.
altar: Joseph, sold by his brothers, later fed them with bread in the famine. Christ, betrayed for silver, feeds his brothers and sisters with the Bread of life at every Mass.

2027-02-27.title: Saturday of the Second Week of Lent
readings: You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea
The Lord is kind and merciful
This brother of yours was dead and has come to life
2027-02-27.alt: Lenten weekday. The Gloria and the Alleluia are omitted throughout Lent. Liturgical colour: violet. Commemoration of St Gregory of Narek, abbot and Doctor of the Church (its collect may be used).
2027-02-27.verse: So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
theo: The prophet Micah ends his book with a prayer and a song of wonder. He asks God to shepherd his people “as in the days of old,” and then breaks out: “Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity and passing over the transgression of the remnant of your possession? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency.” God does not merely tolerate forgiving; he delights in it. “You will cast all our sins into the depths of the sea.” Sins thrown into the deepest sea are not fished out again. The Psalm adds its own picture: “as far as the east is from the west, so far he removes our transgressions from us.” And it gives us today's refrain: the LORD is merciful and gracious, slow to anger and abounding in steadfast love.

Then Jesus tells the parable that has brought more sinners home than perhaps any other page of Scripture. The Pharisees and scribes grumble: “This fellow welcomes sinners and eats with them.” So he tells of a father with two sons. The younger demands his inheritance, as if his father were already dead, and wastes it in a distant country. When famine comes he feeds pigs and longs for their pods. Then “he came to himself” and says: “I will get up and go to my father.” He rehearses a speech, but the father does not let him finish. “While he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.” Robe, ring, sandals, the fatted calf: the son is restored, not as a hired hand but as a son. Then the elder son, who never left home, refuses to come in. The father goes out to him too: “Son, you are always with me, and all that is mine is yours.” The story ends with the question hanging in the air: will he come in? Both sons are lost; both are loved. Today we also remember St Gregory of Narek, the tenth-century Armenian monk and Doctor of the Church, whose Book of Lamentations is a long prayer “speaking with God from the depths of the heart,” the prayer of a sinner who trusts the Father's mercy more than his own sin.
outline: Ask: have you ever been welcomed back when you did not deserve it?
Point 1 · Who is a God like you?
The God who delights in mercy.
He came to himself, and the father ran.
The lost son who never left home.
“This brother of yours was dead and has come to life.”
live: Go to the Father (Luke 15:18)
Make your Lenten confession, perhaps this weekend.
Come in to the feast
If you are the elder brother in some story, take the first step to rejoice with someone who has come back.
2027-02-27.prayer: Father of mercies, you run to meet us while we are still far off. Bring us home from every distant country, cast our sins into the depths of the sea, and free us from the resentment of the elder son. Through the prayers of St Gregory of Narek, teach us to speak with you from the depths of our hearts. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
altar: The father said: let us eat and celebrate. The Eucharist is the feast the Father prepares for every child who comes home.

quick: Forty days after his birth Jesus is presented in the temple.
Simeon takes him in his arms: my eyes have seen your salvation.
He is a light for the nations and a sign that will be opposed.
2027-02-02.action: Light a blessed candle at family prayer tonight.
2027-02-02.question: Have I presented my whole life to God, or only parts of it?
catechism: The Presentation of Jesus in the temple.
kidsaint: Two old people who waited in the temple for many years to see God's promised Saviour. When Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus, they knew him at once and praised God. Lesson: if we pray and wait, God lets us see him!
2027-02-02.special: Feast of the Presentation of the Lord (Candlemas). World Day for Consecrated Life.
term: The traditional English name of today's feast, from the blessing of candles. The candles remind us that Christ is the light of the world.

family.explain: Mary and Joseph brought baby Jesus to the temple. An old man named Simeon took him in his arms and thanked God, because he saw that this baby was the Saviour, the light for all people.
family.intention: We pray for all priests, sisters and brothers who have given their lives to God.
family.ask: Ask: “How can our family be a light for others this week?”

illus: An illustration

In a convent in Kollam an old sister, nearly ninety, could no longer teach or nurse. Each morning she sat in the chapel with a small candle beside her and prayed for every name the other sisters brought her. A young novice asked whether she missed working. She smiled: I am Anna now. I never leave the temple. Someone must keep the light burning while the others go out.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, light of the nations, you came to your temple in the arms of Mary. Come to us now and make us your light. Amen.
share: The Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple (Malachi 3:1). Am I seeking him?
My eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:30). Where have I seen God's salvation?
A sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:35). What sorrow can I unite with Mary's?
pm.resp: Christ, light of the world, shine on us.
interc: For the Church, that she may carry Christ's light to all nations.
For all consecrated men and women, on their world day.
For the elderly who wait in faith, like Simeon and Anna.
For mothers and newborn children.
For our group, that we may offer our lives to God.
pm.close: Father, your Son was presented in the temple as the light of the nations. Purify our hearts and present us to you, burning with his light. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Job cries out in his long night of suffering.
Jesus takes a sick woman by the hand, lifts her up, and she serves.
Jesus prays in the dark and goes on to proclaim the message everywhere.
2027-02-07.action: Visit, call or pray with a sick person this week.
2027-02-07.question: Whose hand does Jesus want me to take this week?
catechism: The sacrament of the Anointing of the Sick.
kidsaint: A girl from Sudan who was kidnapped and sold as a slave, and treated very cruelly. Later she met Jesus, became free and became a religious sister in Italy. She forgave everyone and was always kind. Her feast is tomorrow. Lesson: Jesus can heal even the deepest hurts!
2027-02-07.special: Fifth Sunday in Ordinary Time. Last Sunday before Lent.
term: The sacrament in which a priest anoints the seriously ill or elderly with blessed oil, praying for strength, peace, forgiveness and, if God wills, healing of the body (James 5:14–15).

family.explain: Peter's mother-in-law was sick with a fever. Jesus took her hand and helped her up, and she was well! Then she got up and served everyone.
family.intention: We pray for all who are sick, and for doctors and nurses.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is sick that we can visit or pray for this week?”

illus: An illustration

A palliative-care nurse in Kottayam works night shifts with patients who cannot sleep for pain. She says many ask her the question of Job: when will this night end? She cannot always take away the pain. But she holds their hands, and some tell her that a hand held in the dark is the first time they have felt God near. She calls her work the Capernaum shift.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, healer of the sick and hope of the sleepless, take us by the hand and lift us up. Amen.
share: Nights of misery are apportioned to me (Job 7:3). Whom do I know who is living through a long night?
He took her by the hand and lifted her up (Mark 1:31). How has Jesus lifted me?
Woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel (1 Corinthians 9:16). Do I feel any urgency to share my faith?
pm.resp: Lord, heal the brokenhearted.
interc: For the sick, the dying and those in pain, especially before the World Day of the Sick.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers.
For those who suffer depression and sleepless nights.
For the Church as we prepare to begin Lent.
For our group, that healed by Christ we may serve.
pm.close: God of all consolation, your Son came to the door of every sufferer. Heal us, raise us, and send us to serve and to proclaim. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God set his bow in the clouds as a sign of his covenant with all creation.
The ark prefigured baptism, which now saves us through the risen Christ.
Jesus was tempted in the desert and proclaimed: repent, and believe.
2027-02-14.action: Choose a daily time of silence for the forty days.
2027-02-14.question: What is the desert God is leading me into this Lent, and what temptation must I face there?
catechism: The temptations of Jesus in the desert.
Noah's ark, a figure of Baptism.
kidsaint: Two brothers who went far away to tell people about Jesus. The people there had no letters to write their language, so the brothers made an alphabet and wrote the Bible for them! Lesson: we can help everyone hear about Jesus in a way they understand.
2027-02-14.special: First Sunday of Lent. Rite of Election. Sts Cyril and Methodius not kept this year.
term: Catechumens who have been chosen by the bishop at the Rite of Election, usually on the First Sunday of Lent, to receive Baptism, Confirmation and the Eucharist at the Easter Vigil.

family.explain: The Holy Spirit led Jesus into the desert for forty days. Satan tempted him, but Jesus said no to Satan. Wild animals were near, and angels took care of him. Then Jesus said: turn back to God and believe the good news!
family.intention: We pray for people who will be baptized at Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for us to say no to something wrong? Let us ask Jesus for help.”

illus: An illustration

A young mother in Thiruvalla was preparing for Baptism at Easter. On the First Sunday of Lent she stood before the bishop as her name was called and written in the Book of the Elect. She said afterwards: for months I felt alone in my desert of questions. Today I heard my name, and I knew the whole Church was walking with me to the water.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were tempted in the desert and overcame. Lead us through our forty days by your Spirit. Amen.
share: I have set my bow in the clouds (Genesis 9:13). Do I trust God's covenant of peace?
Baptism… now saves you (1 Peter 3:21). How do I live my baptism?
He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan (Mark 1:13). What is my temptation?
pm.resp: Your ways, O Lord, are love and truth.
interc: For the elect, who will be baptized at Easter.
For all who face strong temptation.
For the care of creation, God's covenant partner.
For people in the deserts of loneliness, illness or doubt.
For our group, that we may keep a faithful Lent.
pm.close: Father, your Son was tempted and overcame. Make us strong in him through these forty days. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Abraham is ready to give God his only son, and God provides a ram instead.
God did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all.
Jesus is transfigured, and the Father says: This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!
2027-02-21.action: Spend ten minutes each day this week listening to Jesus in the Gospel.
2027-02-21.question: What is the Isaac in my life that God is asking me to trust to him?
catechism: Abraham's faith tested; God provides the lamb.
God did not spare his own Son.
kidsaint: When he was a little boy, his mother and father died, and he was sent to look after pigs. One day he found a coin. He was very poor, but instead of buying something for himself, he gave it to a priest to pray at Mass for his father. Later he became a great saint and a cardinal. Lesson: even when we have little, we can give it to God!
2027-02-21.special: Second Sunday of Lent. St Peter Damian not kept this year.
term: Hebrew for “binding”: the Jewish name for the story of Abraham binding Isaac on Mount Moriah (Genesis 22), which Christians read as a figure of the sacrifice of Christ.

family.explain: Jesus took three friends up a high mountain. Suddenly his face and clothes shone bright white! Moses and Elijah were there. Then God the Father spoke from a cloud: This is my Son, whom I love. Listen to him!
family.intention: We pray for everyone who finds it hard to listen to Jesus.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we listen to Jesus better as a family this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A widow in Changanassery had only one son, an engineer with a good job. One day he told her he wanted to become a priest and go as a missionary to Africa. She cried for a week. Then, on a Sunday when this reading from Genesis was proclaimed, she went to the parish priest and said: I have been holding my Isaac too tightly. At his ordination she gave him her hands to anoint first. She says now that she has never felt so close to her son as since the day she gave him back.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, beloved Son of the Father, lead us up the mountain, show us your glory, and teach us to listen to you. Amen.
share: Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love (Genesis 22:2). What is God asking me to entrust to him?
He who did not withhold his own Son (Romans 8:32). Do I believe God will give me everything with him?
This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him! (Mark 9:7). How do I listen to Jesus?
pm.resp: I will walk before the Lord, in the land of the living.
interc: For parents who have lost a child, and for those who have given their children to God.
For all who are tested in faith.
For the elect preparing for baptism at Easter.
For priests and religious, that their lives may reflect the transfigured Christ.
For our group, that we may listen to Jesus and follow him to the cross.
pm.close: Father, you commanded us to listen to your beloved Son. Open our ears and our hearts, and let his glory sustain us on the way to Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God gave the Ten Commandments to a people he had set free.
Jesus cleansed the Temple and spoke of the temple of his body.
We proclaim Christ crucified, the power and wisdom of God.
2027-02-28.action: Make an examination of conscience with the Ten Commandments, and go to confession.
2027-02-28.question: Which tables in the temple of my heart does Jesus need to overturn?
catechism: The Ten Commandments in the covenant.
Christ crucified, the power of God.
kidsaint: A monk in Armenia, long ago, who loved to talk to God from his heart. He wrote a big book of prayers, telling God honestly about his sins and trusting God's love even more. Lesson: we can talk to God about everything, even our mistakes.
2027-02-28.special: Third Sunday of Lent. First Scrutiny of the elect; the Year A readings may be used where there are catechumens.
term: A rite celebrated with the elect on the Third, Fourth and Fifth Sundays of Lent: the community prays over them to heal what is weak and sinful and strengthen what is good, before their Baptism at Easter.

family.explain: Jesus went to the Temple, God's house, and found people buying and selling and shouting. He drove them out and said: do not make my Father's house a market! Jesus wants God's house, and our hearts too, to be places of prayer and love.
family.intention: We pray for the people who will be baptized at Easter.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we make our home and our hearts a place where Jesus is happy to stay?”

illus: An illustration

A parish in Kottayam started a Lenten practice: phones in a basket at the church door, silence for ten minutes before Mass. At first people grumbled. By the Third Sunday an old man said: for years I came to church like going to the market. Now I come in and hear my own heart, and I hear God.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, zeal for your Father's house consumed you. Cleanse our hearts and make them your temple. Amen.
share: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out… of the house of slavery (Exodus 20:2). From what slavery has God freed me?
Stop making my Father's house a marketplace (John 2:16). Where do I bargain with God?
We proclaim Christ crucified (1 Corinthians 1:23). Do I find the cross foolish or powerful?
pm.resp: Lord, you have the words of everlasting life.
interc: For the elect at their First Scrutiny, that Christ may free and fill them.
For the Church, that she may be a house of prayer for all peoples.
For those enslaved by money, pleasure or addiction, that Christ may set them free.
For lawmakers, that just laws may protect life, family and the poor.
For our group, that we may keep God's commandments with love.
pm.close: Father, you gave us your Son as the true temple. Make us living stones in him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: The heroes of faith suffered, yet they believed.
Jesus frees the man called Legion with one word.
The healed man is sent home to tell of God's mercy.
2027-02-01.action: Tell one person at home something the Lord has done for you.
2027-02-01.question: What does the Lord want me to tell my own family about his mercy?

family.explain: Jesus healed a man who was very sick in his mind. The man wanted to go with Jesus, but Jesus said: go home and tell your family what God has done for you!
family.intention: We pray for people who are troubled in their minds and hearts.
family.ask: Ask: “What good thing has God done for our family that we can thank him for?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from a coastal village near Alappuzha spent three years in the grip of alcohol and drugs. His mother said he was like a stranger who shouted at walls. After a retreat and long treatment he came home. The parish priest suggested he join a mission team in another town, but he said: first I must sit at my mother's table and let her see that God gave her son back. That was his first sermon.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are stronger than every evil that binds us. Make us whole and send us to tell of your mercy. Amen.
share: Of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). Whose faithfulness do I remember with gratitude?
My name is Legion; for we are many (Mark 5:9). What divides me inside?
Tell them how much the Lord has done for you (Mark 5:19). Whom should I tell?
pm.resp: Lord, have mercy on us and make us whole.
interc: For persecuted Christians, the faithful of whom the world is not worthy.
For those troubled in mind, and for their families.
For those bound by addiction.
For doctors, counsellors and priests who bring healing.
For our group, that we may witness first at home.
pm.close: Father, your Son sends the healed back to their homes as witnesses. Make our homes places where your mercy is told and seen. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God disciplines us as a Father, for our holiness.
Nazareth took offense at the carpenter, the son of Mary.
Unbelief closes the door to God's power.
2027-02-03.action: Encourage someone who is tired of a long struggle.
2027-02-03.question: Have I taken Jesus for granted because he is familiar?

family.explain: Jesus went home to Nazareth. The people said: he is only the carpenter, we know his mother! They did not believe, so Jesus could not do many miracles there.
family.intention: We pray for anyone who is sick, especially with a throat or chest illness, through St Blaise.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we listen to Jesus with new ears this week?”

illus: An illustration

A woman in Kozhikode had attended Mass every Sunday for forty years and admitted she rarely listened to the Gospel: she knew it already. During a long illness her grandson read the Gospels aloud to her each evening. She said afterwards: I had known Jesus the way the people of Nazareth knew the carpenter. In the hospital I met him for the first time.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, son of Mary, carpenter of Nazareth, open our eyes to see you as you are, and heal our unbelief. Amen.
share: The Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:6). Can I see my hardships as training?
Is not this the carpenter? (Mark 6:3). Where do I take Jesus for granted?
He was amazed at their unbelief (Mark 6:6). What would amaze Jesus about my faith?
pm.resp: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief.
interc: For those whose struggles have made them tired or bitter.
For the sick, especially those with illnesses of the throat, through St Blaise.
For the Church in Scandinavia and northern Europe, through St Ansgar.
For families, that they may see Christ in the ordinary.
For our group, that we may listen with fresh hearts.
pm.close: Father, your Son was rejected in his own town. Give us faith that welcomes him every day. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: We have come not to frightening Sinai but to joyful Zion.
Jesus sends the Twelve two by two.
They travel light, call to repentance and heal the sick.
2027-02-04.action: Invite a friend to join you in one act of service this week.
2027-02-04.question: What baggage keeps me from going where Jesus sends me?

family.explain: Jesus sent his friends out in pairs to tell people about God. They did not take money or food, only a stick for walking. They trusted God to take care of them.
family.intention: We pray for missionaries all over the world.
family.ask: Ask: “Who could we visit together to bring them God's love?”

illus: An illustration

Two retired schoolteachers in a parish near Thiruvananthapuram began visiting housebound elderly people every Thursday. They took nothing but a small Bible and a bottle of water. One said: alone I would have given up after a month. Together we have kept going for six years. Jesus knew what he was doing when he sent them out in twos.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you send us out as you sent the Twelve. Give us courage, companions and trust. Amen.
share: You have come to Mount Zion (Hebrews 12:22). Do I see Mass as heaven's festival?
Two by two (Mark 6:7). Who is my companion in mission?
Nothing for their journey except a staff (Mark 6:8). What can I leave behind?
pm.resp: Lord, send us out in your name.
interc: For missionaries and catechists.
For the sick, and for priests who anoint them.
For those who travel far from home for work.
For the Church in India, through St John de Britto.
For our group, that we may serve together.
pm.close: Father, you sent your Son and he sent his apostles. Send us too, light and trusting, to bring your Kingdom near. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Let mutual love and hospitality continue.
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today and forever.
Herod feared his guests; John and St Agatha feared only God.
2027-02-05.action: Welcome a stranger or newcomer today.
2027-02-05.question: Where do I act like Herod, knowing the truth but fearing what others think?

family.explain: God says: I will never leave you. Jesus is the same yesterday, today and forever. He was with St Agatha when she was brave, and he is with us too.
family.intention: We pray for women and girls who suffer violence, through St Agatha.
family.ask: Ask: “When is it hard for us to be brave for Jesus?”

illus: An illustration

A young woman working in a Bengaluru office was told by her manager that her promotion depended on spending a weekend away with him. She refused and was moved to a lesser post. A year later she said: I lost a title, but I kept myself. When I read about St Agatha I realised that saints are not only in old books.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the same yesterday, today and forever. Give us the courage of St John the Baptist and St Agatha. Amen.
share: Do not neglect to show hospitality (Hebrews 13:2). Whom can I welcome?
I will never leave you or forsake you (Hebrews 13:5). Do I believe this?
Out of regard for his oaths and for the guests (Mark 6:26). Whose opinion rules me?
pm.resp: The Lord is my light and my salvation.
interc: For women and girls who suffer violence or harassment.
For those suffering from breast cancer and all who care for them, through St Agatha.
For prisoners, and for those who visit them.
For leaders, that they may not fear people more than truth.
For our group, that we may stand firm in faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave St Agatha courage to keep faith and purity unto death. Make us faithful in small things and great. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Offer God a sacrifice of praise and of sharing.
Jesus invites tired apostles to rest, then has compassion on the crowd.
St Paul Miki and companions died on crosses at Nagasaki, forgiving.
2027-02-06.action: Take fifteen quiet minutes alone with the Lord today.
2027-02-06.question: Do I make time to rest with Jesus, and do I have compassion for the crowd?

family.explain: The apostles were very tired, so Jesus said: come and rest. But many people came, and Jesus felt sorry for them because they were like sheep without a shepherd. So he taught them.
family.intention: We pray for Christians in Japan and all of Asia, through St Paul Miki.
family.ask: Ask: “How can we rest with Jesus this Sunday?”

illus: An illustration

A Japanese Catholic visiting Kerala told a parish youth group about her great-great-grandparents, hidden Christians near Nagasaki. For generations they baptised their babies secretly and prayed before a statue that looked like a Buddhist goddess but was really Mary. She said: we had no priests for two hundred and fifty years, yet the Shepherd kept us. Do not take your Sunday Mass for granted.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Good Shepherd, give us rest in you, compassion for others, and courage like the martyrs of Japan. Amen.
share: Let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise (Hebrews 13:15). Is my life a song of praise?
Come away… and rest a while (Mark 6:31). Do I let Jesus refresh me?
He had compassion for them (Mark 6:34). For whom should I have compassion?
pm.resp: The Lord is my shepherd; I shall not want.
interc: For Christians persecuted in Asia, through St Paul Miki and companions.
For the Church in Japan.
For pastors and all who are worn out in service.
For those who are like sheep without a shepherd.
For our group, that we may rest in Christ and serve with compassion.
pm.close: Father, you strengthened the martyrs of Nagasaki on their crosses. Make us faithful unto death and generous unto all. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.
God saw that it was good.
All who touched the fringe of Jesus' cloak were healed.
2027-02-08.action: Pray by name for one sick person today.
2027-02-08.question: Do I see creation as God's gift, and do I bring my wounds to Jesus' touch?

family.explain: At the very beginning everything was dark. God said: Let there be light! And there was light. Everything God made is good.
family.intention: We pray for people who are sick, and for children who are not free.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one thing God made that you love? Let us thank him for it.”

illus: An illustration

A teacher in Alappuzha took her catechism class to the lake shore before dawn. They sat in silence until the sun came up over the water. Then she read slowly: God said, let there be light. A boy whispered: it is like watching the first day. She told them: every morning is God saying it again.

pm.open: Creator God, you spoke and there was light. Speak your light into our hearts tonight. Amen.
share: Let there be light (Genesis 1:3). Where do I need God's light?
God saw that it was good (Genesis 1:10). Do I thank God for his creation?
That they might touch even the fringe of his cloak (Mark 6:56). Whom can I bring to Jesus?
pm.resp: Lord, how manifold are your works!
interc: For the care of God's creation and for those who protect it.
For the sick in our parish and families.
For victims of human trafficking, through St Josephine Bakhita.
For doctors, nurses and caregivers.
For our group, that we may praise God in all things.
pm.close: Father, all your works are good. Heal what is broken in us and in the world, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God created humankind in his image, male and female.
God blessed the seventh day and made it holy.
Jesus warns: honour God with the heart, not only the lips.
2027-02-09.action: Choose your three Lenten resolutions tonight.
2027-02-09.question: Is my faith only on my lips, or in my heart?

family.explain: God made people last, and he made us like himself! Every person is special because God's image is in them.
family.intention: We pray for people who are treated as if they are not important.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us do for Jesus this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

In a hospital ward in Kozhikode a nurse was asked why she spoke so gently to a patient who could no longer speak or move. She answered: my grandmother taught me that God's face is hidden in every face. This man is still God's image. He deserves my best words.

pm.open: Lord, you made us in your image. Turn our hearts back to you as Lent begins. Amen.
share: In the image of God he created them (Genesis 1:27). Do I see God's image in others?
God blessed the seventh day (Genesis 2:3). Do I keep Sunday holy?
Their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6). Where is my heart far from God?
pm.resp: Lord, how majestic is your name!
interc: For respect for every human life from conception to natural death.
For married couples, that they may reflect God's image together.
For workers who have no day of rest.
For those who care for elderly parents.
For our group, that our Lent may be a true return of the heart.
pm.close: Father, crown us again with your glory, and make our worship true. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Return to the Lord with all your heart; rend your hearts, not your clothing.
Be reconciled to God; now is the acceptable time.
Give, pray and fast in secret; your Father sees and rewards.
2027-02-10.action: Keep today's fast and give what you save to the poor.
2027-02-10.question: What does God want me to change, from the heart, this Lent?
catechism: Interior penance and its many forms.
Lent and Jesus' forty days in the desert.
The precept of fasting and abstinence.
kidsaint: The twin sister of St Benedict. She loved to talk with God and about God. Once she prayed and a storm came so that her brother had to stay and keep talking about heaven with her! Lesson: Lent is a time to talk with God more.
2027-02-10.special: Ash Wednesday: beginning of Lent, day of fasting and abstinence, blessing and imposition of ashes.
term: Latin for “the fortieth”: the ancient name for Lent, the forty days of preparation for Easter, from Ash Wednesday to the Mass of the Lord's Supper on Holy Thursday.

family.explain: Jesus says: when you do good, do not show off. Give quietly, pray quietly in your room, and God your Father, who sees everything, will be happy with you.
family.intention: We pray that our whole family may grow closer to Jesus this Lent.
family.ask: Ask: “What will each of us give up, and what will each of us give, this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A schoolboy in Kollam put his Lenten savings in a tin marked only with a cross. At Easter his mother found it heavy with coins and asked what it was for. He said: Father told us to give in secret, so I did not tell you. Together they took it to the parish for a family whose house had burnt down. The family never learnt who had given it.

pm.open: Lord, we are dust, yet you love us. Tear open our hearts and turn them to you this Lent. Amen.
share: Rend your hearts and not your clothing (Joel 2:13). What outward show do I hide behind?
Now is the acceptable time (2 Corinthians 6:2). What have I been postponing with God?
Your Father who sees in secret (Matthew 6:6). Do I do good to be seen?
pm.resp: Have mercy, O Lord, for we have sinned.
interc: For the whole Church, that this Lent may be a true return to God.
For catechumens preparing for Baptism at Easter.
For the hungry, who fast without choosing to.
For those far from God, that they may hear: be reconciled.
For our group, that we may pray, fast and give together.
pm.close: Father, gracious and merciful, receive our Lent and lead us to the joy of Easter. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God sets before us life and death: choose life.
Follow Jesus by taking up your cross daily.
Our Lady of Lourdes, health of the sick, pray for us.
2027-02-11.action: Accept one cross today without complaint, and offer it for a sick person.
2027-02-11.question: Which daily cross am I trying to avoid instead of carrying with Jesus?

family.explain: Jesus says: if you want to follow me, carry your cross every day. A cross can be doing a hard job without grumbling, or being kind when it is difficult.
family.intention: We pray for all sick people, through Our Lady of Lourdes.
family.ask: Ask: “What is one small cross each of us can carry for Jesus today?”

illus: An illustration

A retired bus conductor from Ernakulam went to Lourdes with a parish pilgrimage, hoping his damaged legs would be healed. They were not. But he came home saying: at the grotto I stopped asking why me. I saw hundreds of sick people praying for each other. I learnt to carry my cross with Jesus. That was my miracle.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you call us to take up our cross daily. Give us courage, and through your Mother comfort the sick. Amen.
share: Choose life (Deuteronomy 30:19). What choice is before me now?
Take up their cross daily (Luke 9:23). What is my daily cross?
What does it profit them? (Luke 9:25). What am I tempted to gain at the cost of my soul?
pm.resp: Mary, health of the sick, pray for us.
interc: For the sick, especially those who suffer alone.
For doctors, nurses and all who care for the sick.
For pilgrims at Lourdes and at Marian shrines in India.
For those facing a hard choice between right and wrong.
For our group, that we may carry our crosses with love this Lent.
pm.close: Father, your Son carried his cross to give us life. Help us to follow him with Mary. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God rejects fasting that ignores the poor and oppresses workers.
The true fast frees the oppressed and shares bread with the hungry.
We fast in longing for Jesus, the Bridegroom.
2027-02-12.action: Share a meal or the money saved by fasting with someone hungry.
2027-02-12.question: Does my fasting make me kinder and more just?

family.explain: God says: the best fasting is sharing food with hungry people, giving homes to people who have none, and giving clothes to people who need them.
family.intention: We pray for poor and hungry families.
family.ask: Ask: “What can our family share with someone in need this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A parish youth group in Palakkad decided to skip their Friday snacks in Lent. Each week they cooked the money into a pot of rice and curry and took it to migrant workers at a construction site. One worker asked why. A girl answered: because God says the fast he likes is sharing bread. The worker said: then today your God has fed me.

pm.open: Lord, teach us the fast you choose: hearts that share and hands that set free. Amen.
share: Why do we fast, but you do not see? (Isaiah 58:3). Is my fasting only outward?
To share your bread with the hungry (Isaiah 58:7). With whom can I share?
Then they will fast (Matthew 9:15). Do I fast out of love for Jesus?
pm.resp: A broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
interc: For the hungry and the homeless.
For workers who are underpaid or unpaid.
For those held in any kind of bondage.
For employers, that they may be just.
For our group, that our fasting may become sharing.
pm.close: Father, make our fasting a light that breaks forth like the dawn. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Remove the pointing finger and the speaking of evil.
The merciful will be like a watered garden.
Jesus came to call sinners: Levi got up and followed.
2027-02-13.action: Give up criticism and gossip for one whole day.
2027-02-13.question: Where am I still sitting at my tax booth, unwilling to get up and follow?

family.explain: Levi took money unfairly, and people did not like him. But Jesus said: follow me! Levi left everything and had a big party for Jesus. Jesus is like a doctor who comes for sick people.
family.intention: We pray for people who feel too bad to come back to God.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone we have been unkind about? How can we be kind to them?”

illus: An illustration

A man in Kannur had not been to church for thirty years and ran a shop known for cheating customers. One Lent the parish priest stopped at his counter, bought something and said: come and see me, I want to talk. The man came. After confession he began paying back customers he had cheated. He said: I thought the Church was for good people. Then I learnt it is a hospital.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Doctor of our souls, you came for sinners. We come to you as we are. Heal us. Amen.
share: The pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil (Isaiah 58:9). Whom do I criticise?
You shall be like a watered garden (Isaiah 58:11). Where do I need God's water?
He got up, left everything, and followed him (Luke 5:28). What must I leave?
pm.resp: Teach me your way, O Lord.
interc: For sinners who feel unwelcome in the Church.
For those who hear confessions, that they may be ministers of mercy.
For tax collectors and all in public finance, that they may be honest.
For people who criticise and those who are hurt by criticism.
For our group, that we may welcome sinners as Jesus did.
pm.close: Father, your Son ate with sinners. Seat us at his table and heal us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God says: be holy, for I am holy; do not cheat, lie or hold a grudge.
On the last day Jesus will judge us by our care for the least.
Whatever we do to the poor, we do to Christ.
2027-02-15.action: Do one work of mercy this week for someone who cannot repay you.
2027-02-15.question: In whose face is Jesus waiting for me this Lent?

family.explain: Jesus says: when you give food to a hungry person, or visit someone who is sick, you are doing it for me! Jesus hides in people who need help.
family.intention: We pray for hungry people, sick people and people in prison.
family.ask: Ask: “Who needs our help this week? How can we help Jesus in that person?”

illus: An illustration

A retired bank clerk in Thrissur began visiting the district jail with a prison ministry group one Lent. He expected to give advice. Instead an old prisoner asked him to sit and listen while he talked about the son who never came. The clerk went home and could not sleep. He said later: I went to visit a prisoner, and the Lord was there before me, waiting to be visited. He has gone every month since.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, King of glory, you hide yourself in the least of your brothers and sisters. Open our eyes to see you and our hands to serve you. Amen.
share: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy (Leviticus 19:2). Where does holiness need to reach in my daily dealings?
You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge (Leviticus 19:18). Is there a grudge I carry?
You did it to me (Matthew 25:40). When did I last meet Christ in someone poor?
pm.resp: Lord, make us holy, as you are holy.
interc: For the hungry, the homeless and refugees.
For the sick and those who care for them.
For prisoners and their families, and for prison ministers.
For employers and workers, that wages may be just and paid on time.
For our group, that our Lent may be full of works of mercy.
pm.close: Father, your Son will come in glory to judge the living and the dead. Help us to serve him now in the least, that we may be welcomed into the kingdom prepared for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God's Word is like rain: it always brings fruit.
Jesus teaches us not to babble but to trust the Father.
In the Our Father we promise to forgive as we are forgiven.
2027-02-16.action: Pray the Our Father slowly, and forgive one person by name.
2027-02-16.question: Which word of God has been falling on me without my letting it sink in?

family.explain: Jesus taught his friends to pray to God as our Father. We do not need many words, because God already knows what we need. And we promise to forgive others as God forgives us.
family.intention: We pray for families who find it hard to forgive.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to forgive before we say the Our Father tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A grandmother in a village near Pala prayed the Our Father with her family every night for fifty years. When her eldest son quarrelled with his brother over land and stopped coming home, she kept praying it, but she began to stop at “as we forgive those who trespass against us” and wait in silence. One evening the son, visiting for her birthday, heard the silence and asked why. She said: I am waiting for you to finish the sentence. The next week he went to see his brother.

pm.open: Father, your Word does not return to you empty. Let it fall on us like rain and bear fruit. Amen.
share: It shall not return to me empty (Isaiah 55:11). Where has God's Word borne fruit in my life?
Your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:8). Do I trust him?
As we also have forgiven our debtors (Matthew 6:12). Whom do I still need to forgive?
pm.resp: Our Father, forgive us as we forgive.
interc: For all who read and preach the Word of God.
For those who have stopped praying.
For families divided by quarrels over property or money.
For farmers waiting for rain and harvest.
For our group, that the Our Father may shape our lives.
pm.close: Father, your Son taught us to call you by name. Keep us faithful to his prayer and generous in forgiving. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God gives Jonah a second chance, and Jonah preaches to Nineveh.
The whole city, from the king down, repents and God relents.
Jesus is the sign greater than Jonah: he died and rose on the third day.
2027-02-17.action: Fix a date for confession this Lent.
2027-02-17.question: What is the one evil way God is asking me to turn from?

family.explain: Jonah told the people of Nineveh that they must change. Everyone, from the king to the little children, said sorry to God and stopped doing wrong. And God forgave them!
family.intention: We pray for everyone who needs to say sorry to God this Lent.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we need to say sorry for as a family, and how can we change?”

illus: An illustration

A businessman in Kochi had cheated his partners for years and grown rich. During a Lenten retreat he heard the story of the king of Nineveh who stood up from his throne and sat in ashes. He said afterwards: I realised that I had never once stood up from my throne. He went to confession, then visited each partner he had wronged, and began repaying what he could. It took him nine years. He says the first day of repayment was the first day he slept in peace.

pm.open: Lord God, you are slow to anger and rich in mercy. Turn our hearts to you, and give us a second chance. Amen.
share: The word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time (Jonah 3:1). When has God given me a second chance?
Everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5). How can our family repent together?
Something greater than Jonah is here (Luke 11:32). Do I still let Christ move me?
pm.resp: A broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
interc: For all who need to repent, that they may hear God's call.
For leaders, that like the king of Nineveh they may humble themselves before God.
For cities full of violence.
For the Servite Order and all who honour Our Lady of Sorrows.
For our group, that our Lent may be a true turning.
pm.close: Father, the Ninevites turned at Jonah's word. Make us turn at the word of your Son, who died and rose for us. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Queen Esther, alone and in danger, prays to God for courage and help.
Jesus says: ask, search, knock; the Father gives good things.
Treat others as you want to be treated.
2027-02-18.action: Bring God the request you have been afraid to ask.
2027-02-18.question: Do I pray as a child who trusts the Father, or as a stranger who doubts?

family.explain: Jesus says: ask God, and he will give you what is good. If Mummy and Daddy give good things to their children, God our Father gives even better things!
family.intention: We pray for people who are afraid and alone.
family.ask: Ask: “What do we want to ask God for together tonight?”

illus: An illustration

A nurse from Kottayam working in the Gulf found herself trapped by an employer who took her passport and would not pay her. She had no family nearby and no one to call. She said later that she prayed only one line, over and over: Lord, I have no helper but you. A Malayali priest she met at Sunday Mass put her in touch with the embassy. Three months later she was home. She now volunteers with a group that helps migrant workers in the same trouble.

pm.open: Lord, you are our King and our only help. Hear us when we call, and give us courage. Amen.
share: Help me, who am alone and have no helper but you (Esther C:14). When did I last pray like this?
Ask, search, knock (Matthew 7:7). Do I give up too easily in prayer?
Do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). Whom have I treated as I would not want to be treated?
pm.resp: Lord, on the day I called for help, you answered me.
interc: For persecuted minorities and peoples in danger.
For migrant workers who are exploited and alone.
For women in positions of risk and responsibility.
For those who have stopped believing that God hears them.
For our group, that we may pray with persistence and trust.
pm.close: Father, you give good things to those who ask you. Make us bold in prayer and generous in charity. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God wants the sinner to turn and live, not to die.
Jesus asks for a heart free of anger and contempt.
Before offering a gift at the altar, be reconciled first.
2027-02-19.action: Take the first step towards reconciliation with someone today.
2027-02-19.question: Who has something against me, and what is stopping me from going to them?

family.explain: Jesus says: if you have hurt someone, go and make peace with them first, and then come to pray and give your gift to God.
family.intention: We pray for families and friends who are not speaking to each other.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there anyone we need to say sorry to or make peace with?”

illus: An illustration

Two neighbours in a village near Kannur had not spoken for twelve years after a quarrel over a boundary wall. One Lenten Friday the parish priest read this Gospel at Mass. One of the men left the church before Communion, walked across the lane, and knocked on his neighbour's door. They both came back to church together for the evening Way of the Cross. The wall is still there, but now there is a small gate in it.

pm.open: Lord, there is forgiveness with you. Turn our hearts and make us peacemakers. Amen.
share: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked? (Ezekiel 18:23). Do I believe anyone can change, even me?
If you are angry with a brother or sister (Matthew 5:22). What anger do I carry?
First be reconciled (Matthew 5:24). To whom must I go?
pm.resp: If you, O Lord, should mark iniquities, Lord, who could stand?
interc: For those who have lost hope of changing.
For families and neighbours divided by quarrels.
For victims of violence and for those who have done violence.
For those who feel trapped by the sins of their parents.
For our group, that we may be first to seek reconciliation.
pm.close: Father, you desire that all turn and live. Make us instruments of your peace. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God and Israel make a covenant: you are my treasured people.
Jesus says: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.
Be perfect in love, as the Father is perfect.
2027-02-20.action: Pray by name for someone who has hurt you.
2027-02-20.question: Whom have I excluded from my love, and what would it take to include them?

family.explain: Jesus says: love even the people who are unkind to you, and pray for them. God makes the sun shine on everyone, good and bad. We are his children, so we must love like him.
family.intention: We pray for people who are unkind to us.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone who is unkind to us whom we can pray for tonight?”

illus: An illustration

In 1999 Graham Staines, an Australian missionary who had cared for leprosy patients in Odisha for decades, was burned to death with his two young sons by a mob. A few days later his widow, Gladys, told the press that she had forgiven the killers and had no bitterness. She stayed on in India for years to continue the work among leprosy patients. Many in India who had never read the Gospel said they understood what Jesus meant by loving enemies when they heard her words.

pm.open: Father, you are kind to the good and the evil. Make us your children, perfect in love. Amen.
share: Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people (Deuteronomy 26:18). Do I know that I am God's treasure?
Love your enemies (Matthew 5:44). Who is my enemy?
Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Where does my love stop short?
pm.resp: Happy are those who walk in the law of the LORD.
interc: For those who persecute Christians, that they may meet Christ.
For victims of violence, that they may find healing and the grace to forgive.
For nations and communities divided by hatred.
For catechumens preparing for baptism at Easter.
For our group, that we may love without exception.
pm.close: Father, your Son prayed for those who crucified him. Give us his heart, that we may love as you love. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Peter confessed Jesus as the Messiah, the Son of the living God.
Jesus named him Rock and gave him the keys of the kingdom.
Peter's successor still strengthens the Church in one faith.
2027-02-22.action: Pray today for the Pope and for your bishop by name.
2027-02-22.question: If Jesus asked me today, “Who do you say that I am?”, what would I honestly answer?
catechism: Peter's confession and the keys of the kingdom.
The Pope, successor of Peter, source of unity.
The Church, the flock of the one Shepherd.
kidsaint: A fisherman who loved Jesus very much, but sometimes was afraid and made mistakes. Once he even said he did not know Jesus! But Jesus forgave him and made him the leader of the apostles. Lesson: Jesus can make us strong, even when we are weak.
2027-02-22.special: The Chair of St Peter, Apostle. Feast in Lent: Gloria said, no Alleluia.
term: The bishop's chair, a sign of his office of teaching and shepherding. The church where it stands is the cathedral. The Chair of Peter stands for the teaching office of the Pope.

family.explain: Jesus asked his friends: who do you say I am? Peter answered: you are the Christ, the Son of the living God! Jesus was happy and said: you are Peter, the rock. I will build my Church on you. Today the Pope takes Peter's place and helps the whole Church stay together.
family.intention: We pray for the Pope and our bishop.
family.ask: Ask: “Who is Jesus for each one of us? Let everyone say one thing.”

illus: An illustration

A teacher in a Kottayam school showed her class a photo of the great bronze Chair in St Peter's Basilica. One boy said: but nobody sits in it! She smiled: exactly. It is too big for anyone. It reminds every Pope that he only keeps the seat for Jesus, and that his strength comes from Christ's prayer, not his own.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, Son of the living God, you built your Church on the rock of Peter. Keep us united in faith and love. Amen.
share: But who do you say that I am? (Matthew 16:15). Who is Jesus for me now?
You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church (Matthew 16:18). How do I love and pray for the Church?
Tend the flock of God… willingly (1 Peter 5:2). Whom am I called to care for?
pm.resp: The Lord is my shepherd; there is nothing I shall want.
interc: For our Holy Father the Pope, that the Lord may keep his faith firm.
For our bishop and all the shepherds of the Church.
For Christians who are divided, that we may be one.
For those who are losing their faith, that someone may strengthen them.
For our group, that we may confess Jesus with Peter's faith.
pm.close: Father, you gave Peter the keys of the kingdom. Keep us in the one flock of your Son. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.
