quick: God invites sinners: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow.
Jesus warns against saying and not doing.
St Polycarp served Christ eighty-six years and died faithful.
2027-02-23.action: Do one hidden act of service today that no one will thank you for.
2027-02-23.question: Where does my faith stop at words and fail to become action?

family.explain: Jesus says: the greatest person is the one who serves others. People who show off will be brought low, but people who are humble will be lifted up by God.
family.intention: We pray for priests and teachers, that they may live what they teach.
family.ask: Ask: “How can each of us serve someone at home today without being asked?”

illus: An illustration

An old catechism teacher in a parish near Alappuzha was known to the children for one thing: she never asked them to do anything she did not do first. When she taught them to visit the sick, she took them with her to the homes of the bedridden. Years later a former pupil, now a priest, said: I forgot most of her lessons, but I never forgot her feet walking to those houses.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, one Teacher and Master, you came to serve. Wash us and make us humble servants. Amen.
share: Cease to do evil, learn to do good (Isaiah 1:16–17). What good do I need to learn?
They do not practice what they teach (Matthew 23:3). Where do my words outrun my life?
The greatest among you will be your servant (Matthew 23:11). Whom can I serve this week?
pm.resp: To the upright I will show the saving power of God.
interc: For pastors and teachers, that they may live what they teach.
For the oppressed, orphans and widows, that justice may reach them.
For those who think their sins are too great to be forgiven.
For persecuted Christians, through the prayers of St Polycarp.
For our group, that our faith may be humble and practical.
pm.close: Father, you make scarlet sins white as snow. Teach us to serve as your Son served. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Jeremiah was repaid with evil for the good he did, and still prayed.
James and John asked for honours; Jesus offered them his cup.
The Son of Man came to serve and to give his life as a ransom.
2027-02-24.action: Take the last place or the hardest task today, quietly.
2027-02-24.question: Where am I still seeking the first place, even in my faith or my service?

family.explain: Two of Jesus' friends wanted to be the most important. Jesus said: the most important one is the one who serves everyone. Jesus came to serve us and even gave his life for us.
family.intention: We pray for people who serve others quietly: cleaners, nurses, cooks, drivers.
family.ask: Ask: “Who serves our family every day? How can we thank them?”

illus: An illustration

At a parish feast in Thrissur, the committee members were arguing about who would sit on the stage with the bishop. Meanwhile an elderly man nobody knew was washing the plates behind the hall. When the bishop arrived, he went to the kitchen first, greeted the old man, and took a towel. The committee members quietly followed him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you came not to be served but to serve. Give us your humble heart. Amen.
share: Is evil a recompense for good? (Jeremiah 18:20). How do I respond when I am repaid with ingratitude?
Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? (Matthew 20:22). What cup is Jesus offering me?
Whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant (Matthew 20:26). Whom am I called to serve?
pm.resp: Save me, O Lord, in your steadfast love.
interc: For those who are persecuted for speaking the truth.
For leaders in Church and society, that they may serve and not dominate.
For those who serve in hidden ways, that God may reward them.
For mothers who pray for their children's future.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus to Jerusalem.
pm.close: Father, your Son gave his life as a ransom for many. Make us servants after his heart. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Those who trust in the Lord are like a tree planted by water.
The rich man's sin was that he never saw Lazarus at his gate.
Listen to God's word now; the chasm is fixed after death.
2027-02-25.action: Learn the name of one poor person you see regularly, and help them.
2027-02-25.question: Who is lying at my gate, unseen?

family.explain: Jesus told a story about a rich man who had a big feast every day. A poor man named Lazarus was hungry and sick at his gate, but the rich man never helped him. Jesus wants us to see people who need help and share with them.
family.intention: We pray for poor and hungry families near our home.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone near us who needs help? What can our family share this Lent?”

illus: An illustration

A software engineer in Kakkanad walked past the same old man every morning at the bus stop. One Lenten Thursday, after hearing this Gospel, she stopped and asked his name. It was Lazar. She laughed, then cried. Now she brings him breakfast every Thursday, and he prays for her family. She says: he was at my gate for two years, and I never saw him.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you were poor for our sake. Open our eyes to the poor at our gate and root our hearts in you. Amen.
share: Blessed are those who trust in the LORD (Jeremiah 17:7). Where are my roots?
At his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus (Luke 16:20). Who is at my gate?
If they do not listen to Moses and the prophets (Luke 16:31). Am I really listening to God's word?
pm.resp: Happy are they who hope in the Lord.
interc: For the poor and the sick who lie unseen at the gates of the rich.
For the rich and comfortable, that they may open their eyes and hearts.
For those who trust only in money or power, that they may turn to God.
For farmers and all who wait for rain in the dry season.
For our group, that we may share generously this Lent.
pm.close: Father, you hear the cry of the poor. Make us see and share, through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: Joseph, the beloved son, was sold by his envious brothers; God turned it to good.
The tenants killed the owner's son to seize the vineyard.
The rejected stone, Christ, has become the cornerstone.
2027-02-26.action: Pray the Way of the Cross today, or pause at three o'clock to remember the Passion.
2027-02-26.question: Where is envy or possessiveness keeping me from welcoming the Son?

family.explain: Joseph's brothers were jealous because their father loved him so much. They sold him to traders. But God was with Joseph and later used him to save his whole family. Jesus too was rejected, but God made him our Saviour.
family.intention: We pray for families where brothers and sisters are fighting.
family.ask: Ask: “When do we feel jealous of each other? Let us say sorry and pray for each other.”

illus: An illustration

Two brothers in Kuttanad stopped speaking for twelve years over a strip of paddy land left by their father. One Lent, the younger brother heard the story of Joseph at Mass. That Friday he walked to his elder brother's house with the land documents and said: take it; I want my brother more than my field. They prayed the Way of the Cross together that evening.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, rejected stone and cornerstone, free us from envy and make us bear fruit for you. Amen.
share: They hated him, and could not speak peaceably to him (Genesis 37:4). With whom do I find it hard to speak peaceably?
This is the heir; come, let us kill him (Matthew 21:38). Do I treat the Lord's vineyard as my own?
The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone (Matthew 21:42). Do I trust God to bring good out of rejection?
pm.resp: Remember the marvels the Lord has done.
interc: For families divided by envy, property and inheritance.
For people sold and trafficked, that they may be set free.
For those who are rejected and despised, that they may know Christ's company.
For the Church, that she may bear fruit in due season.
For our group, that we may follow Jesus on the Way of the Cross.
pm.close: Father, you made the rejected stone the cornerstone. Bring good out of all our trials. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

quick: God delights in mercy and casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
The father ran to his lost son and restored him as a son.
He went out to the elder son too: both are called to the feast.
2027-02-27.action: Go to confession this weekend, or fix the day for it.
2027-02-27.question: Am I more like the younger son, far from home, or the elder son, near but resentful?

family.explain: A son ran away and wasted all his money. When he came back, sad and hungry, his father ran to him, hugged him and kissed him, and made a big party. God is like that father. He always welcomes us back when we say sorry.
family.intention: We pray for people who are far from God, that they may come home.
family.ask: Ask: “Is there someone in our family we need to forgive and welcome back?”

illus: An illustration

A young man from Kollam left home angry and did not call his parents for three years. One Lenten Saturday he took a bus home, rehearsing his apology all the way. When he reached the lane, his mother was already standing at the gate. She said: I have stood here every evening since you left. He never finished his speech.

pm.open: Father of mercies, you run to meet us. Bring us home and teach us to rejoice when others come home. Amen.
share: Who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? (Micah 7:18). Do I believe God delights to forgive me?
I will get up and go to my father (Luke 15:18). What keeps me from going?
Son, you are always with me (Luke 15:31). Do I resent God's mercy to others?
pm.resp: The Lord is kind and merciful.
interc: For those far from home and far from God, that they may come to themselves.
For parents waiting for children who have gone away.
For priests who hear confessions, that they may welcome like the father.
For those who feel resentful and left out, that they may come in to the feast.
For our group, that we may be merciful as the Father is merciful.
pm.close: Father, you rejoice over every child who returns. Make us glad with you. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, through the prophet Malachi God promised: the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple (Malachi 3:1). Israel expected a king in glory. Today the Lord comes to his temple as a little child, carried in his mother's arms.

Mary and Joseph come to fulfil the law. They bring the offering of the poor, a pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons (Luke 2:24). The one who will be the true Lamb is redeemed with the gift of the poor. God enters our world through humility and obedience.

Simeon, guided by the Spirit, takes the child in his arms and sings: Master, now you are dismissing your servant in peace… for my eyes have seen your salvation (Luke 2:29–30). An old man holds the One who holds the universe. That is why we carry candles today: Christ is a light for revelation to the Gentiles.

But Simeon also tells Mary: this child is destined for the falling and the rising of many… and a sword will pierce your own soul too (Luke 2:34–35). The light will shine from the cross. Mary offers her Son today and will offer him again on Calvary.

Anna, a widow of eighty-four, never left the temple but worshiped there with fasting and prayer night and day (Luke 2:37). Today we thank God for all consecrated men and women who, like Anna, give their whole lives to him.

Hebrews says he became like us in every respect, so that he might be a merciful and faithful high priest (Hebrews 2:17). Let us present ourselves to him today, and carry his light into every dark place. Amen.
kids: Children, Mary and Joseph took baby Jesus to God's house. Old Simeon held him and said: this baby is the light for the whole world!
When you see a candle in church, remember: Jesus is our light. Let us shine for him.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Job speaks for everyone who has lain awake in pain: when I lie down I say, ‘When shall I rise?’ But the night is long, and I am full of tossing until dawn (Job 7:4). God's Word does not hide this cry. It gives words to our suffering.
The Psalm answers: he heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds (Psalm 147:3). The God who counts the stars bends down to bandage a wound.

In the Gospel, Jesus enters Simon's house. Simon's mother-in-law lies with a fever. He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them (Mark 1:31). Healed, she serves. Every grace we receive is meant to become service.

By evening the whole city was gathered around the door (Mark 1:33). And before dawn, while it was still very dark, Jesus went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed (Mark 1:35). The healer draws his strength from the Father in the dark.

When the disciples say everyone is searching for you, he answers: let us go on to the neighboring towns, so that I may proclaim the message there also (Mark 1:38). Paul says: woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel! (1 Corinthians 9:16).

This week Lent begins, and on Thursday we pray with the sick on the feast of Our Lady of Lourdes. Let us take someone by the hand: visit the sick, pray in the early hours, and share the Good News. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus held the hand of a sick lady and helped her up, and she was well! Then she helped everyone else.
Let us pray for sick people this week, and maybe visit someone who is sick with Mummy or Daddy.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, every First Sunday of Lent takes us into the desert with Jesus. This year Mark tells it in just two verses: the Spirit immediately drove him out into the wilderness. He was in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan; and he was with the wild beasts; and the angels waited on him (Mark 1:12–13).

Israel was tested forty years in the wilderness and failed. Adam was tested in a garden and fell. Jesus, the new Adam and the true Israel, is tested and stands firm. And around him are wild beasts at peace and angels serving: a glimpse of paradise restored.

In the first reading God makes a covenant with Noah and with every living creature, and sets his bow in the clouds as a sign (Genesis 9:13). The bow, a weapon of war, now hangs in the sky as a sign of peace.

St Peter tells us that the ark, in which eight persons were saved through water, prefigured baptism, which now saves you (1 Peter 3:20–21). Christ suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, to bring us to God. Today the elect, who will be baptized at Easter, are called by name.

Then Jesus proclaims: the time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news (Mark 1:15). That is Lent in one sentence: turn around, and trust the good news.

We do not enter this desert alone. The Spirit leads us, the angels serve us, and Jesus, who was tempted as we are, goes ahead of us. Let us pray with the Psalm: make me to know your ways, O LORD. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus stayed in the desert for forty days. Satan tried to make him do wrong, but Jesus said no! Angels came to help him.
When you are tempted to do something wrong, say: Jesus, help me! He will help you say no.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, after these things God tested Abraham. He said, take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love… and offer him there as a burnt offering (Genesis 22:1–2). Every word of that command is heavy. Isaac was the gift of God, the son of the promise.

Abraham went. He built the altar, laid the wood, bound his son and took the knife. Then the angel called: do not lay your hand on the boy… for now I know that you fear God, since you have not withheld your son, your only son, from me (Genesis 22:12). God did not want Isaac's death. He wanted Abraham's whole heart.

St Paul looks at Calvary and says: he who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else? (Romans 8:32). What God spared Abraham, he did not spare himself. On Moriah a ram was found; on Golgotha the Son himself is the Lamb.

In the Gospel Jesus leads Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and he was transfigured before them, and his clothes became dazzling white (Mark 9:2–3). They see for a moment the glory of the one who will soon be rejected and crucified.

Then a cloud overshadowed them, and the Father said: this is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him! (Mark 9:7). And suddenly they saw no one with them any more, but only Jesus (Mark 9:8). The vision passes; Jesus remains. That is enough.

This Lent, let us offer God our Isaac, whatever we hold too tightly, and trust that he will provide. And let us listen to his Son every day. The light of the mountain will carry us through the cross to Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus took three friends up a mountain, and his clothes became shining white! Then God the Father said: this is my Son, I love him, listen to him!
This week, let us listen to Jesus: read a little bit of the Gospel each day with Mummy or Daddy.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, today's first reading begins: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery (Exodus 20:2). Before God gives a single commandment, he reminds Israel: I have set you free. The Ten Commandments are not chains. They are the road map of freedom.
That is why the Psalm can say the law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul, sweeter also than honey. And we answer with Peter: Lord, you have the words of everlasting life.

In the Gospel Jesus goes into the Temple and finds a market. He makes a whip of cords, overturns the tables and says: stop making my Father's house a marketplace! (John 2:16). His disciples remember: zeal for your house will consume me.

Then he says: destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up (John 2:19). He was speaking of the temple of his body. The true meeting place of God and humanity is Jesus himself, crucified and risen. And by baptism we are built into him.

St Paul says: we proclaim Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles, but to those who are the called, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God (1 Corinthians 1:23–24). The cross looks weak, but it is stronger than all human strength.

This Lent, let Jesus walk into the temple of your heart. Let him overturn the tables where you bargain with God, drive out the idols, and make your heart a house of prayer. And let us pray for the elect at their scrutinies, that they may come to the living water at Easter. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus went to God's house and found people buying and selling and making noise. He said: this is my Father's house, a place to pray!
Our hearts are God's house too. Let us keep them clean by saying sorry and saying our prayers.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews closes its list of the heroes of faith: time would fail me to tell of Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, of David and Samuel and the prophets (Hebrews 11:32). Some shut the mouths of lions; others were tortured, stoned and killed by the sword.
Faith does not always look like victory. Some escaped and some died, and all were faithful: people of whom the world was not worthy (Hebrews 11:38). And they wait to be made perfect together with us.

In the Gospel Jesus meets a man whom no chain could hold, living among the tombs. His name is Legion, for we are many (Mark 5:9). Evil tears a person into pieces. One word of Jesus, and the man sits clothed and in his right mind (Mark 5:15).

He wants to follow Jesus, but Jesus says: go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you (Mark 5:19). Our first mission field is our own home. Let us tell our families of his mercy. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus made a very sick man well, and then said: go home and tell your family what God has done for you! Tonight, tell your family one good thing God did for you today.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells a tired community: my child, do not regard lightly the discipline of the Lord, or lose heart when you are punished by him; for the Lord disciplines those whom he loves (Hebrews 12:5–6). Our hardships are not signs that God has left us.

Discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness (Hebrews 12:11). So lift your drooping hands, pursue peace, and let no root of bitterness spring up.

In Nazareth the people said: is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary? And they took offense at him (Mark 6:3). They thought they knew him, so they could not receive him. He could do no deed of power there, and he was amazed at their unbelief.

We too can take Jesus for granted because we have known him since childhood. Today, through the prayers of St Blaise, let us ask for healing of body and soul, and ask for new eyes to see the Lord. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nazareth said: he is only the carpenter! They did not believe in Jesus. Let us always listen to Jesus as if we are hearing him for the first time.

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews tells us we have not come to Sinai with its fire, darkness and trumpet. You have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering (Hebrews 12:22).
We have come to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speaks a better word than the blood of Abel (Hebrews 12:24). Every Mass is this festival of heaven.

In the Gospel Jesus called the twelve and began to send them out two by two (Mark 6:7). They took nothing but a staff. They preached repentance, cast out demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them (Mark 6:13).
We too are sent, not alone but together, not loaded with baggage but trusting in God. Let us go from this Mass two by two to bring his healing. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus sent his friends out in pairs to help people and tell them about God. Who can you go with to do something kind this week?

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says: let mutual love continue. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it (Hebrews 13:1–2). Remember prisoners, honour marriage, keep free from the love of money.
Why can we live like this? Because he has said: I will never leave you or forsake you (Hebrews 13:5). Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever (Hebrews 13:8).

In the Gospel Herod liked to listen to John, yet out of regard for his oaths and for the guests he ordered his death (Mark 6:26). He knew the truth but feared people more than God. John, in chains, was the free man.

Today we honour St Agatha, the young martyr of Sicily, who chose Christ over safety and purity over the will of a powerful man. The Christ who strengthened her is the same today. Let us ask for her courage. Amen.
kids: Children, St Agatha was a brave girl who loved Jesus more than anything. Even when she was hurt, she stayed faithful. Jesus helps us to be brave too!

homily: Dear friends, Hebrews says: through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name (Hebrews 13:15). And do not neglect to do good and to share what you have.

It blesses us: may the God of peace, who brought back from the dead our Lord Jesus, the great shepherd of the sheep… make you complete in everything good so that you may do his will (Hebrews 13:20–21).

In the Gospel Jesus tells his tired apostles: come away to a deserted place all by yourselves and rest a while (Mark 6:31). But seeing the crowd, he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd (Mark 6:34).

Today we honour St Paul Miki and his companions, crucified at Nagasaki in 1597. From the cross Paul Miki preached and forgave. Let us rest in the Good Shepherd and, like the martyrs, give our lives with compassion. Amen.
kids: Children, St Paul Miki and his friends in Japan, even young boys, loved Jesus so much that they died on crosses, singing and forgiving. Let us pray for children everywhere who suffer for Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, today we begin to read the first page of the Bible: in the beginning when God created the heavens and the earth (Genesis 1:1). Darkness covered the deep, and God said: let there be light; and there was light (Genesis 1:3).

Day after day God gives order and life, and again and again we hear: God saw that it was good. Creation is not a god to be feared or worshipped; it is a gift from the one good God. Even the sun and moon are lamps he has hung in the sky.

In the Gospel the people of Gennesaret run through the whole region bringing their sick to Jesus. They beg to touch even the fringe of his cloak, and all who touch it are healed (Mark 6:56). The Word who made all things now walks among us and heals.

Today we may remember St Josephine Bakhita, sold as a child slave, who found in Jesus a Master who loved her. Let us thank God for his creation, bring our sick to Jesus, and pray for all who are not free. Amen.
kids: Children, God said: Let there be light! And there was light. Everything God made is good, and you are good too! Let us say thank you to God.

homily: Dear friends, today the creation story reaches its summit: God said, let us make humankind in our image, according to our likeness (Genesis 1:26). Only of us is this said.

So God created humankind in his image, male and female he created them (Genesis 1:27). Every person bears God's image: the child in the womb, the poor man at the gate, the old woman in her bed. Then God rested on the seventh day and blessed it. Our work finds its meaning in rest and worship.

In the Gospel Jesus quotes Isaiah: this people honours me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me (Mark 7:6). Some had used religious customs to avoid caring for their own parents. Jesus says: you abandon the commandment of God and hold to human tradition (Mark 7:8).
Tomorrow is Ash Wednesday. Lent asks one thing: give God your heart, not only your lips. Let us choose tonight how we will pray, fast and give, and let God restore his image in us. Amen.
kids: Children, God made you like himself! That is why every person is special. This Lent, let us love Jesus with our hearts, not only with our words.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, Lent begins with a trumpet. The prophet Joel cries out: yet even now, says the LORD, return to me with all your heart, with fasting, with weeping, and with mourning; rend your hearts and not your clothing (Joel 2:12–13).

Why return? Not because God is harsh, but because he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love (Joel 2:13). And Joel calls everyone: elders and children, the newly married and the priests. Lent is the whole Church coming home together.

Paul pleads with us: we entreat you on behalf of Christ, be reconciled to God (2 Corinthians 5:20). He who knew no sin was made sin for us, so that in him we might become the righteousness of God. And he adds: see, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation! Not next year. Today.

Jesus gives us three works: almsgiving, prayer and fasting. But he warns: do not do them to be seen. Give so quietly that your left hand does not know what your right hand is doing; pray in your room with the door shut; fast with a washed face. And your Father who sees in secret will reward you (Matthew 6:4, 6, 18).

In a moment we will receive ashes. The priest will say: repent, and believe in the Gospel, or: remember that you are dust, and to dust you shall return. The ashes are not a decoration. They are an honest confession: we are sinners, we are mortal, and we need God's mercy.

Yet dust in God's hands is never just dust. From dust he formed Adam; from the dust of the tomb he will raise us. Let us begin these forty days with torn-open hearts, hidden love and great hope. Amen.
kids: Children, today we get a cross of ashes on our foreheads. It reminds us that we need Jesus and that we want to love him more.
For Lent, choose one way to pray more, one thing to give up, and one way to help someone, and do it quietly for Jesus.

homily: Dear friends, Moses sets a choice before Israel: I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live (Deuteronomy 30:19). Lent begins with this same choice.

Jesus shows us the road to life. The Son of Man must suffer, be rejected, be killed and on the third day be raised. Then he says to all: if any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me (Luke 9:23).

Daily. Not one great sacrifice, but small faithful choices: patience at home, honesty at work, kindness to the difficult. And Jesus asks: what does it profit them if they gain the whole world, but lose or forfeit themselves? (Luke 9:25).

Today we remember Our Lady of Lourdes and pray for the sick on the World Day of the Sick. At Lourdes Mary asked for prayer and penance. Many have been healed; many more have received strength to carry their cross. With Mary, let us choose life by following Jesus on the way of the cross. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: carry your cross every day. That means doing hard good things with love. Mary helps us, like she helped St Bernadette at Lourdes. Let us pray for sick people today!

homily: Dear friends, God tells Isaiah: shout out, do not hold back! The people fast and complain that God does not notice. God replies: you serve your own interest on your fast day, and oppress all your workers (Isaiah 58:3).

Then God describes the fast he chooses: to loose the bonds of injustice, to let the oppressed go free, to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house (Isaiah 58:6–7). Fasting without mercy is empty.

And the promise: then your light shall break forth like the dawn; you shall call, and the LORD will answer, here I am (Isaiah 58:8–9). In the Gospel Jesus says his disciples will fast when the bridegroom is taken away (Matthew 9:15). We fast because we long for him.
On this first Friday of Lent, let our abstinence be love: for Jesus the Bridegroom, who was taken away on the cross, and for the poor in whom he waits for us. Amen.
kids: Children, God says the best kind of fasting is sharing. If we give up a sweet this Lent, let us use it to help someone who is hungry!

homily: Dear friends, Isaiah promises: if you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil, if you offer your food to the hungry, then your light shall rise in the darkness (Isaiah 58:9–10).

The Lord will guide you continually, and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water, whose waters never fail (Isaiah 58:11). Small sins like gossip and blame dry us up; mercy makes us a garden.

Jesus sees Levi, a tax collector, and says: follow me. And he got up, left everything, and followed him (Luke 5:27–28). When the Pharisees complain, Jesus says: those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance (Luke 5:31–32).
Lent is not for perfect people. It is for the sick who know they need the Doctor. Let us get up from wherever we are sitting, and follow Jesus, beginning with a good confession. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus called Levi, even though people did not like him, and Levi followed Jesus. Jesus is like a doctor for our hearts. When we do wrong, we can always go back to him.

homily: Dear friends, on this first Monday of Lent God speaks to Moses: you shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy (Leviticus 19:2). And then, surprisingly, he talks about wages, lies, slander and grudges.

Holiness is not far away. It is in paying the labourer on time, in not putting a stumbling block before the blind, in refusing to hate in our heart. The commandment ends: you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD (Leviticus 19:18).

In the Gospel Jesus shows us the last day. The King will say: I was hungry and you gave me food, I was a stranger and you welcomed me, I was sick and you took care of me, I was in prison and you visited me (Matthew 25:35–36). Both the blessed and the cursed are surprised. Neither saw him.

Lent is a time to open our eyes. Just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me (Matthew 25:40). Let us look for Christ this week in someone poor, sick or forgotten. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: when you share your food or visit a sick friend, you are doing it for me! This week, do one kind thing for someone who needs help, and remember that Jesus is hiding there.

homily: Dear friends, God says through Isaiah: as the rain and the snow come down from heaven, and do not return there until they have watered the earth… so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty (Isaiah 55:10–11).
We hear many words every day. God's Word is different: it does what it says. Let us give it room this Lent, a few minutes each day with the Gospel, and trust that it will bear fruit in its own time.
In the Gospel Jesus says: do not heap up empty phrases… your Father knows what you need before you ask him (Matthew 6:7–8). Then he teaches us the Our Father. It is the prayer of children who trust.
Jesus explains only one line of it: if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you (Matthew 6:14). Today, before we pray it, let us forgive someone by name. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus taught us a special prayer: the Our Father. Tonight, say it slowly with your family, and when you say “as we forgive those who trespass against us”, think of someone you can forgive.

homily: Dear friends, the word of the LORD came to Jonah a second time (Jonah 3:1). That is good news: God does not give up on us after our first failure.

Jonah enters Nineveh and cries: forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown! (Jonah 3:4). And the people of Nineveh believed God; they proclaimed a fast, and everyone, great and small, put on sackcloth (Jonah 3:5). Even the king stood up from his throne and sat in ashes.
God saw what they did, how they turned from their evil ways, and he did not bring the calamity (Jonah 3:10). Repentance is not just feeling sorry; it is turning, with our hands as well as our hearts.

Jesus says the only sign he will give is the sign of Jonah: his death and resurrection. See, something greater than Jonah is here! (Luke 11:32). If the pagans turned at five words, how much more should we turn at the word of Christ. Amen.
kids: Children, the people of Nineveh were doing many bad things. When Jonah told them to change, they all said sorry to God, even the king! And God forgave them. God always forgives us when we are truly sorry.

homily: Dear friends, Queen Esther knew her people were about to be destroyed. Before going to the king, she lay on the ground in prayer: O my Lord, you only are our king; help me, who am alone and have no helper but you (Esther C:14).
She did not pretend to be strong. She remembered God's faithfulness and asked for courage and the right words. And God turned the king's heart. Prayer from the depths is never wasted.

Jesus says: ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you (Matthew 7:7). If you then, who are evil, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your Father in heaven give good things to those who ask him! (Matthew 7:11).
And Jesus adds: in everything do to others as you would have them do to you (Matthew 7:12). Let us ask the Father with trust today, and then give to others what we hope to receive. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: ask God for what you need, and he will give you good things, because he is your Father. Tonight, ask God for something for someone else, and trust him.

homily: Dear friends, the exiles said: we are paying for our parents' sins; nothing we do matters. Ezekiel answers with God's word: if the wicked turn away from all their sins… they shall surely live; they shall not die (Ezekiel 18:21).
God asks: have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked… and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live? (Ezekiel 18:23). No one is too far gone. Lent is always a time of hope.

Jesus asks us for a deeper righteousness. Murder begins with anger and insult. So when you are offering your gift at the altar, if you remember that your brother or sister has something against you, leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled (Matthew 5:23–24).
Today we abstain from meat. Let us also abstain from anger, and go first to someone we have hurt. That is the gift God most wants from us this Friday. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: if you have hurt someone, go and make peace first. Is there a brother, sister or friend you need to say sorry to today? Go and say it, and God will be very happy!

homily: Dear friends, Moses tells Israel: today you have obtained the LORD's agreement: to be your God… Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people (Deuteronomy 26:17–18). It is like a marriage vow between God and his people.
At baptism we made the same covenant. We are God's treasured people. Lent is the time to say again, today: I am yours, and I will walk in your ways.

Jesus shows us how far God's ways reach: love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you, so that you may be children of your Father in heaven; for he makes his sun rise on the evil and on the good (Matthew 5:44–45).

Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect (Matthew 5:48). Not flawless, but complete in love. As this first week of Lent ends, let us pray by name for the one person we find hardest to love. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says: love even people who are unkind to you, and pray for them. The sun shines on everyone! Tonight, pray for someone who was not nice to you.

homily: Dear brothers and sisters, in the middle of Lent we put on white and celebrate the Chair of St Peter. We do not honour a chair. We honour the mission Christ gave to a fisherman: to teach, to guide and to hold the Church together in one faith.

At Caesarea Philippi Jesus asked: who do people say that the Son of Man is? Many answers, all too small. Then: but who do you say that I am? (Matthew 16:15). This question comes to each of us. No one can answer it for us.

Simon answered: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. And Jesus said: flesh and blood has not revealed this to you, but my Father in heaven. Faith is a gift. Then he gave him a new name: you are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades will not prevail against it (Matthew 16:18).

Peter was not strong by nature. He tried to keep Jesus from the cross. He denied him three times. But Jesus prayed for him, that his faith would not fail, and told him: strengthen your brothers. The rock is made by grace.

That is why the first reading is so humble. Peter, an old man, calls himself an elder and a witness of the sufferings of Christ, and asks shepherds to tend the flock willingly, not lording it over others but being examples (1 Peter 5:2–3). Authority in the Church is service.

Today let us pray for our Holy Father, for our bishop, for our priests. And let us answer the question of Jesus with Peter's words, from our hearts: you are the Messiah, the Son of the living God. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus gave Simon a new name: Peter, which means rock! Peter was not always brave, but Jesus made him strong and made him the leader of his Church.
Today the Pope helps the Church like Peter did. Let us say a Hail Mary for the Pope today!

homily: Dear friends, God speaks through Isaiah to a people whose temple was busy but whose lives were not changed. Wash yourselves; make yourselves clean… cease to do evil, learn to do good; seek justice, rescue the oppressed, defend the orphan, plead for the widow (Isaiah 1:16–17).

And then the invitation: come now, let us argue it out, says the LORD: though your sins are like scarlet, they shall be like snow (Isaiah 1:18). No sin is too red for God's mercy. Lent is the time to come and reason with him in confession.

In the Gospel Jesus warns us about a faith of display: they do not practice what they teach. They love the best seats and titles. But Jesus says: the greatest among you will be your servant. All who exalt themselves will be humbled, and all who humble themselves will be exalted (Matthew 23:11–12).

Today we remember St Polycarp, bishop of Smyrna and disciple of St John. At eighty-six, when told to curse Christ, he said in substance: for eighty-six years I have served him, and he has done me no wrong; how can I blaspheme my King? He lived what he taught. May we too say and do, for Christ our King. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus says the greatest person is the one who helps others. St Polycarp was a bishop who loved Jesus all his life, even when he was very old. Let us do one kind thing today without being asked!

homily: Dear friends, Jeremiah had prayed for his people, and they plotted to kill him. He cried to God: is evil a recompense for good? Yet they have dug a pit for my life. Remember how I stood before you to speak good for them (Jeremiah 18:20). He is a picture of Jesus, who prayed for those who crucified him.

In the Gospel Jesus tells the Twelve for the third time that he will be condemned and crucified and raised on the third day. And at that very moment the mother of James and John asks for the best seats for her sons. We do the same: we bring Jesus our ambitions while he is speaking of the cross.

Jesus answers: you do not know what you are asking. Are you able to drink the cup that I am about to drink? (Matthew 20:22). The cup is his suffering. Later, James would be the first of the apostles to die as a martyr. He did drink the cup.

Then Jesus teaches all of us: it will not be so among you; whoever wishes to be great among you must be your servant… just as the Son of Man came not to be served but to serve, and to give his life a ransom for many (Matthew 20:26–28). This Lent, let us stop asking for seats and start taking up towels. Amen.
kids: Children, two friends of Jesus wanted to be the most important. Jesus said: the most important person is the one who helps everyone. Jesus came to help us and to give his life for us. Today, help someone at home without being asked!

homily: Dear friends, Jeremiah shows us two trees. One is a shrub in the desert: the person who trusts only in human strength. The other is a tree planted by water: blessed are those who trust in the LORD, whose trust is the LORD (Jeremiah 17:7). In the year of drought it is not anxious, and it does not cease to bear fruit.

Then Jesus tells of a rich man who feasted sumptuously every day, and at his gate lay a poor man named Lazarus, covered with sores (Luke 16:19–20). The rich man did not beat Lazarus. He did not chase him away. He simply did not see him. That was his sin.

Notice: the poor man has a name, Lazarus, God helps. The rich man has no name. In God's eyes the forgotten are remembered. After death the gate the rich man never crossed becomes a great chasm that cannot be crossed.

And Abraham says: if they do not listen to Moses and the prophets, neither will they be convinced even if someone rises from the dead (Luke 16:31). Someone has risen from the dead: Jesus. Let us listen to him today, open our eyes, and cross the gate to Lazarus while there is time. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a rich man who had lots of food but never shared with poor Lazarus at his door. Jesus wants us to see people who need help. Can you share something with someone today?

homily: Dear friends, Israel loved Joseph more than any other of his children, because he was the son of his old age (Genesis 37:3). His brothers hated him. When they saw him coming they said: here comes this dreamer. Come now, let us kill him (Genesis 37:19–20). In the end they sold him for twenty pieces of silver.

Envy is a quiet sin, but it can lead to terrible things. It cannot bear another's good. Yet God was with Joseph. The pit led to Egypt, Egypt to the palace, and the palace to bread for his brothers in the famine. What they meant for evil, God meant for good.

In the Gospel the vineyard owner sends his own son, saying: they will respect my son. But the tenants say: this is the heir; come, let us kill him and get his inheritance (Matthew 21:38). Jesus is telling his own Passion. Like Joseph, he will be sold for silver and handed over.

And yet: the stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this was the Lord's doing (Matthew 21:42). On this Lenten Friday let us stand at the cross and give the Lord the fruit he seeks: a heart without envy, hands that share, and lives that welcome his Son. Amen.
kids: Children, Joseph's brothers were jealous and sold him far away. But God took care of Joseph and turned it all into good. Jesus was also rejected, but God made him our Saviour. When you feel jealous, ask Jesus to give you a happy heart!

homily: Dear friends, Micah asks in wonder: who is a God like you, pardoning iniquity? He does not retain his anger forever, because he delights in showing clemency (Micah 7:18). God does not forgive reluctantly. He delights in it. He casts our sins into the depths of the sea.
Jesus shows us this God in a story. A younger son takes his inheritance and wastes it. When he has nothing left, he comes to himself and says: I will get up and go to my father. He prepares a speech.

But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him (Luke 15:20). The father does not wait. He runs. He does not let the son finish his speech. He gives him a robe, a ring and sandals: you are still my son.

And the elder son, who stayed at home, refuses to come in. The father goes out to him too: son, you are always with me. Today, whether we are the younger son or the elder, the Father is coming out to meet us. St Gregory of Narek prayed: my sins are many, but your mercy is greater (in substance). Let us go home. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus told about a boy who ran away and did wrong things. When he came home, his father ran to him and hugged him and had a party! God is like that father. When we say sorry, he runs to hug us.

intro: Theme: “My eyes have seen your salvation.”
The Lord comes to his temple: the offering of the poor, the light of the nations, the sword.

points.h: The Lord comes to his temple
sub: A child in his mother's arms.
q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Guided by the Spirit, Simeon came into the temple; and when the parents brought in the child Jesus, to do for him what was customary under the law,
points.apply: Visit the Blessed Sacrament this week and greet the Lord in his temple.

q: Consecrate to me all the firstborn; whatever is the first to open the womb among the Israelites, of human beings and animals, is mine.
When the time came for their purification according to the law of Moses, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord
points.apply: Offer your day to God every morning this week.

q: I will give you as a light to the nations, that my salvation may reach to the end of the earth.”
for my eyes have seen your salvation, which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples, a light for revelation to the Gentiles and for glory to your people Israel.”
points.apply: Light a blessed candle at family prayer and pray Simeon's song.

sub: The falling and rising of many.
q: He was despised and rejected by others; a man of suffering and acquainted with infirmity;
and to be a sign that will be opposed so that the inner thoughts of many will be revealed
points.apply: Thank a consecrated person for their life given to God.

concl: The Lord comes in poverty and humility, as light for all peoples.
Let us present our lives to him and carry his light.
2027-02-02.resolve: Pray the Nunc dimittis every night this week.

intro: Theme: “He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.”
Job's night, the healing hand of Jesus, prayer in the dark, and the urgency of the Gospel.

sub: An honest cry in God's Word.
q: When I lie down I say, ‘When shall I rise?’ But the night is long, and I am full of tossing until dawn.
“Come to me, all you that are weary and are carrying heavy burdens, and I will give you rest.
points.apply: Bring your own long night honestly to God in prayer.

points.h: He took her by the hand
q: He heals the brokenhearted, and binds up their wounds.
He came and took her by the hand and lifted her up. Then the fever left her, and she began to serve them.
points.apply: Visit or call a sick person this week.

sub: While it was still very dark.
q: O LORD, in the morning you hear my voice; in the morning I plead my case to you, and watch.
In the morning, while it was still very dark, he got up and went out to a deserted place, and there he prayed.
points.apply: Give God the first ten minutes of each morning.

points.h: Woe to me if I do not proclaim
q: then within me there is something like a burning fire shut up in my bones; I am weary with holding it in, and I cannot.
If I proclaim the gospel, this gives me no ground for boasting, for an obligation is laid on me, and woe to me if I do not proclaim the gospel!
points.apply: Decide on one way to share your faith during Lent.

concl: The Lord who counts the stars binds up our wounds.
Healed by his hand, strengthened by prayer, let us serve and proclaim.
2027-02-07.resolve: Visit a sick person before the World Day of the Sick on 11 February.

intro: Theme: “The time is fulfilled… repent, and believe in the good news.”
The bow of peace, the waters of baptism, the desert of testing and the call to conversion.

q: I have set my bow in the clouds, and it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and the earth.
For in him every one of God's promises is a “Yes.”
points.apply: When you see the sky this week, thank God for his faithfulness.

sub: An appeal for a good conscience.
q: A new heart I will give you, and a new spirit I will put within you; and I will remove from your body the heart of stone and give you a heart of flesh.
For Christ also suffered for sins once for all, the righteous for the unrighteous, in order to bring you to God. He was put to death in the flesh, but made alive in the spirit,
points.apply: Find the date of your baptism and renew your baptismal promises in prayer.

q: Remember the long way that the LORD your God has led you these forty years in the wilderness, in order to humble you, testing you to know what was in your heart, whether or not you would keep his commandments.
For we do not have a high priest who is unable to sympathize with our weaknesses, but we have one who in every respect has been tested as we are, yet without sin.
points.apply: Name your strongest temptation and bring it to Jesus each day.

q: Make me to know your ways, O LORD; teach me your paths.
and saying, “The time is fulfilled, and the kingdom of God has come near; repent, and believe in the good news.”
points.apply: Keep a daily desert of ten minutes' silence with the Gospel.

concl: God's covenant of peace reaches us through the waters of baptism.
Jesus has faced the desert for us; with him we can overcome.
2027-02-14.resolve: Pray each day of Lent for the elect and for your own fidelity to baptism.

intro: Theme: “This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
Abraham's test, the Son not spared, the glory on the mountain, and the one command of the Father.

sub: Your son, your only son, whom you love.
q: He said, “Take your son, your only son Isaac, whom you love, and go to the land of Moriah, and offer him there as a burnt offering on one of the mountains that I shall show you.”
By faith Abraham, when put to the test, offered up Isaac. He who had received the promises was ready to offer up his only son,
points.apply: Offer to God in prayer the person or thing you hold most tightly.

q: Abraham said, “God himself will provide the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” So the two of them walked on together.
He who did not withhold his own Son, but gave him up for all of us, will he not with him also give us everything else?
points.apply: Thank God each night this week for one thing he has provided.

sub: After the first prediction of the Passion.
Glory for the road to the cross.
q: Moses came down from Mount Sinai. As he came down from the mountain with the two tablets of the covenant in his hand, Moses did not know that the skin of his face shone because he had been talking with God.
And he was transfigured before them, and his clothes became dazzling white, such as no one on earth could bleach them.
points.apply: Spend an hour before the Blessed Sacrament this week.

q: The LORD your God will raise up for you a prophet like me from among your own people; you shall heed such a prophet.
Then a cloud overshadowed them, and from the cloud there came a voice, “This is my Son, the Beloved; listen to him!”
points.apply: Read the Sunday Gospel again each day this week and ask: what is Jesus saying to me?

concl: God did not spare his own Son; with him he gives us everything.
The light of the mountain carries us through the cross; the Father's command is simple: listen to him.
2027-02-21.resolve: Spend ten minutes daily with the Gospel for the rest of Lent.

intro: Theme: “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
The Ten Words of freedom, the zeal of Jesus, the temple of his Body and the power of the cross.

sub: Love of God, love of neighbour.
q: I am the LORD your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of slavery; you shall have no other gods before me.
“Do not think that I have come to abolish the law or the prophets; I have come not to abolish but to fulfill.
points.apply: Pray through one commandment each day this week and ask how to keep it with love.

sub: A market in the house of prayer.
The Lord comes to his temple.
q: It is zeal for your house that has consumed me; the insults of those who insult you have fallen on me.

He told those who were selling the doves, “Take these things out of here! Stop making my Father's house a marketplace!” His disciples remembered that it was written, “Zeal for your house will consume me.”
points.apply: Name the table in your heart where you bargain with God, and let Jesus overturn it in confession.

q: See, I am sending my messenger to prepare the way before me, and the Lord whom you seek will suddenly come to his temple.
Jesus answered them, “Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.”
points.apply: Spend ten minutes before the Blessed Sacrament this week, adoring the true temple.

sub: The power and wisdom of God.
q: The law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul; the decrees of the LORD are sure, making wise the simple;
but we proclaim Christ crucified, a stumbling block to Jews and foolishness to Gentiles, but to those who are the called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God.
points.apply: Make the sign of the cross slowly and thoughtfully each morning, as a confession of faith.

concl: God's commandments are the way of freedom; Jesus cleanses and fulfils.
The crucified and risen Body of Christ is the new temple, and we are built into it.
2027-02-28.resolve: Make an examination of conscience with the Ten Commandments and go to confession before Easter.

intro: Theme: “Tell them how much the Lord has done for you.”
The faithful who suffered, the man made whole, and the mission that begins at home.

q: Be strong, and let your heart take courage, all you who wait for the LORD.
of whom the world was not worthy. They wandered in deserts and mountains, and in caves and holes in the ground.
points.apply: Thank God by name for one person whose faith carried yours.

sub: Clothed and in his right mind.
q: he brought them out of darkness and gloom, and broke their bonds asunder.
They came to Jesus and saw the demoniac sitting there, clothed and in his right mind, the very man who had had the legion; and they were afraid.
points.apply: Bring what divides you inside to Jesus in confession.

sub: The first missionary of the Decapolis.
q: Come and hear, all you who fear God, and I will tell what he has done for me.
But Jesus refused, and said to him, “Go home to your friends, and tell them how much the Lord has done for you, and what mercy he has shown you.”
points.apply: Tell one family member what God has done for you.

concl: Faith is faithful whether it escapes the sword or not.
Jesus makes us whole and sends us home as witnesses.
2027-02-01.resolve: Share one story of God's mercy at the family table this week.

intro: Theme: “The Lord disciplines those whom he loves.”
A Father's training, a hometown's unbelief, and faith that sees the Lord afresh.

q: for the LORD reproves the one he loves, as a father the son in whom he delights.
Now, discipline always seems painful rather than pleasant at the time, but later it yields the peaceful fruit of righteousness to those who have been trained by it.
points.apply: Offer one present hardship to God as training in holiness.

q: he had no form or majesty that we should look at him, nothing in his appearance that we should desire him.
Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary and brother of James and Joses and Judas and Simon, and are not his sisters here with us?” And they took offense at him.
points.apply: Read the Gospel this week as if for the first time.

q: As a father has compassion for his children, so the LORD has compassion for those who fear him.
And he could do no deed of power there, except that he laid his hands on a few sick people and cured them. And he was amazed at their unbelief.
points.apply: Make an act of faith before Communion: Lord, I believe.

concl: God's discipline is a Father's love.
Let us welcome Jesus with faith, not with the familiarity that shuts him out.
2027-02-03.resolve: Pray each day this week: Lord, I believe; help my unbelief.

intro: Theme: “He began to send them out two by two.”
The festival of heaven and the mission of the Twelve.

sub: The city of the living God.
Blood that speaks a better word.
q: Now Mount Sinai was wrapped in smoke, because the LORD had descended upon it in fire; the smoke went up like the smoke of a kiln, while the whole mountain shook violently.
But you have come to Mount Zion and to the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem, and to innumerable angels in festal gathering,
points.apply: At Mass this week, join consciously in the song of the angels at the Holy, Holy.

q: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the messenger who announces peace, who brings good news,
He called the twelve and began to send them out two by two, and gave them authority over the unclean spirits.
points.apply: Do one act of service together with a friend.

q: We ponder your steadfast love, O God, in the midst of your temple.
So they went out and proclaimed that all should repent. They cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick and cured them.
points.apply: Visit or call someone who is sick.

concl: At Mass we stand on Zion with angels and saints.
From Mass we are sent, together and trusting, to heal.
2027-02-04.resolve: Visit a sick or lonely person with a companion this week.

intro: Theme: “Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.”
Mutual love, the Lord who never leaves, and the courage of John and St Agatha.

sub: Free from the love of money.
q: you shall love the alien as yourself, for you were aliens in the land of Egypt
Let mutual love continue. Do not neglect to show hospitality to strangers, for by doing that some have entertained angels without knowing it.
points.apply: Welcome one stranger or newcomer this week.

points.h: The same yesterday, today and forever
q: The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid?
Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever.
points.apply: Repeat Hebrews 13:8 whenever you feel afraid.

sub: Trapped by an oath and guests.
q: Do not be afraid of them, for I am with you to deliver you, says the LORD.”
For John had been telling Herod, “It is not lawful for you to have your brother's wife.”
points.apply: Refuse one compromise made only to please others.

concl: Love, hospitality and courage flow from a Lord who never changes.
Like John and St Agatha, let us fear God more than people.
2027-02-05.resolve: Ask St Agatha each day this week for courage and purity of heart.

intro: Theme: “He had compassion for them.”
Praise and sharing, rest with Jesus, and the compassion of the Good Shepherd seen in the martyrs of Nagasaki.

q: Offer to God a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and pay your vows to the Most High.
Through him, then, let us continually offer a sacrifice of praise to God, that is, the fruit of lips that confess his name.
points.apply: Begin and end each day with a short act of praise.

q: He makes me lie down in green pastures; he leads me beside still waters; he restores my soul.
He said to them, “Come away to a deserted place all by yourselves and rest a while.” For many were coming and going, and they had no leisure even to eat.
points.apply: Keep Sunday as a day of rest with the Lord.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD.
As he went ashore, he saw a great crowd; and he had compassion for them, because they were like sheep without a shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
points.apply: Pray for persecuted Christians in Asia, through St Paul Miki.

concl: Our praise and sharing are the sacrifice God desires.
The Good Shepherd gives rest and compassion; the martyrs show the cost of love.
2027-02-06.resolve: Make Sunday a true day of rest and praise this week.

intro: Theme: “All who touched it were healed.”
The good Creator who speaks light into darkness, and the Word made flesh whose touch heals.

q: Then God said, “Let there be light”; and there was light.
For it is the God who said, “Let light shine out of darkness,” who has shone in our hearts to give the light of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
points.apply: Begin each day this week with a short prayer of light: Lord, shine in my heart.

q: O LORD, how manifold are your works! In wisdom you have made them all; the earth is full of your creatures.
Ever since the creation of the world his eternal power and divine nature, invisible though they are, have been understood and seen through the things he has made.
points.apply: Waste less this week: food, water or electricity, as a thank-you to the Creator.

q: But he was wounded for our transgressions, crushed for our iniquities; upon him was the punishment that made us whole, and by his bruises we are healed.
And wherever he went, into villages or cities or farms, they laid the sick in the marketplaces, and begged him that they might touch even the fringe of his cloak; and all who touched it were healed.
points.apply: Visit, call or pray for one sick person by name.

concl: The world is the good gift of a good God.
In Jesus the Creator walks among us and heals.
2027-02-08.resolve: Thank God for one created thing every day this week.

intro: Theme: “Their hearts are far from me.”
Made in God's image, called to worship with the heart, on the eve of Lent.

sub: Only of us is it said.
q: So God created humankind in his image, in the image of God he created them; male and female he created them.
For we are what he has made us, created in Christ Jesus for good works, which God prepared beforehand to be our way of life.
points.apply: Show special respect this week to someone the world overlooks.

q: So God blessed the seventh day and hallowed it, because on it God rested from all the work that he had done in creation.
So then, a sabbath rest still remains for the people of God;
points.apply: Keep next Sunday free for Mass, family and rest.

q: Honor your father and your mother, so that your days may be long in the land that the LORD your God is giving you.
He said to them, “Isaiah prophesied rightly about you hypocrites, as it is written, ‘This people honors me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me;
points.apply: Do one concrete act of care for your parents or elders this week.

concl: We bear God's image; let our worship come from the heart.
Lent begins tomorrow: return to God with the heart.
2027-02-09.resolve: Write down your Lenten resolutions of prayer, fasting and almsgiving tonight.

intro: Theme: “Return to me with all your heart.”
Ash Wednesday: the torn heart, the urgent now, the hidden works, and the dust that God loves.

q: Return to the LORD, your God, for he is gracious and merciful, slow to anger, and abounding in steadfast love, and relents from punishing.
So he set off and went to his father. But while he was still far off, his father saw him and was filled with compassion; he ran and put his arms around him and kissed him.
points.apply: Name one sin you will bring to confession this week.

q: Create in me a clean heart, O God, and put a new and right spirit within me.
For he says, “At an acceptable time I have listened to you, and on a day of salvation I have helped you.” See, now is the acceptable time; see, now is the day of salvation!
points.apply: Do today the act of reconciliation you have been postponing.

q: Prayer with fasting is good, but better than both is almsgiving with righteousness.
But whenever you pray, go into your room and shut the door and pray to your Father who is in secret; and your Father who sees in secret will reward you.
points.apply: Keep one Lenten practice that no one else will know about.

q: By the sweat of your face you shall eat bread until you return to the ground, for out of it you were taken; you are dust, and to dust you shall return.”
Therefore we have been buried with him by baptism into death, so that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we too might walk in newness of life.
points.apply: Each night of Lent, pray: Lord, I am dust; have mercy and make me new.

concl: Lent is the whole Church returning to a gracious Father.
We are dust, but dust in the hands of the God who raises the dead.
2027-02-10.resolve: Write your three Lenten works and keep them daily, in secret.

intro: Theme: “Choose life.”
Two ways, the daily cross, and Mary of Lourdes beside the sick.

sub: Life and death set before us.
q: I call heaven and earth to witness against you today that I have set before you life and death, blessings and curses. Choose life so that you and your descendants may live,
I came that they may have life, and have it abundantly.
points.apply: Each morning of Lent, say: today I choose life; today I choose you, Lord.

sub: The Son of Man must suffer.
q: They are like trees planted by streams of water, which yield their fruit in its season, and their leaves do not wither. In all that they do, they prosper.
Then he said to them all, “If any want to become my followers, let them deny themselves and take up their cross daily and follow me.
points.apply: Name your daily cross and carry it with love this week.

q: As a mother comforts her child, so I will comfort you; you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.
Meanwhile, standing near the cross of Jesus were his mother,
points.apply: Visit or call a sick person this week, and pray a decade of the Rosary for them.

concl: God sets before us life; Jesus shows the way through the cross.
Mary stands with us and with the sick.
2027-02-11.resolve: Offer one daily cross for the sick throughout this week.

intro: Theme: “Is not this the fast that I choose?”
The fast God wants: justice, mercy and longing for the Bridegroom.

q: Look, you fast only to quarrel and to fight and to strike with a wicked fist. Such fasting as you do today will not make your voice heard on high.
Those who say, “I love God,” and hate their brothers or sisters, are liars;
points.apply: Examine how you treat those who work for you or under you.

sub: Do not hide from your own kin.
q: Is it not to share your bread with the hungry, and bring the homeless poor into your house; when you see the naked, to cover them, and not to hide yourself from your own kin?
for I was hungry and you gave me food, I was thirsty and you gave me something to drink, I was a stranger and you welcomed me,
points.apply: Give what you save by fasting to the poor this week.

q: And I will take you for my wife forever; I will take you for my wife in righteousness and in justice, in steadfast love, and in mercy.
And Jesus said to them, “The wedding guests cannot mourn as long as the bridegroom is with them, can they? The days will come when the bridegroom is taken away from them, and then they will fast.
points.apply: When hunger comes today, turn it into a short prayer: Come, Lord Jesus.

concl: True fasting breaks yokes and shares bread.
We fast in love for the Bridegroom and his poor.
2027-02-12.resolve: Keep the Fridays of Lent with abstinence and one act of sharing.

intro: Theme: “I have come to call… sinners to repentance.”
Mercy that makes us a garden, and the Physician who calls the sick.

q: If you remove the yoke from among you, the pointing of the finger, the speaking of evil,
Do not judge, so that you may not be judged.
points.apply: Replace every criticism today with a prayer for that person.

q: The LORD will guide you continually, and satisfy your needs in parched places, and make your bones strong; and you shall be like a watered garden, like a spring of water, whose waters never fail.
The water that I will give will become in them a spring of water gushing up to eternal life.”
points.apply: Do one act of mercy that repairs a broken relationship.

q: I myself will be the shepherd of my sheep, and I will make them lie down, says the Lord GOD. I will seek the lost, and I will bring back the strayed, and I will bind up the injured, and I will strengthen the weak,
Jesus answered, “Those who are well have no need of a physician, but those who are sick; I have come to call not the righteous but sinners to repentance.”
points.apply: Go to confession before the Second Sunday of Lent.

concl: Mercy turns a dry life into a watered garden.
Jesus calls sinners; Lent is for the sick who need him.
2027-02-13.resolve: Give up gossip and criticism for the whole of Lent.

intro: Theme: “Just as you did it to one of the least of these… you did it to me.”
Holiness in daily dealings, a heart without grudges, and Christ hidden in the least.

points.h: Be holy as God is holy
sub: It shows in wages and words.
Every command sealed with his Name.
q: Speak to all the congregation of the people of Israel and say to them: You shall be holy, for I the LORD your God am holy.
instead, as he who called you is holy, be holy yourselves in all your conduct;
points.apply: Examine your work and business dealings for honesty this week.

sub: Do not hate in your heart.
q: You shall not take vengeance or bear a grudge against any of your people, but you shall love your neighbor as yourself: I am the LORD.
Love does no wrong to a neighbor; therefore, love is the fulfilling of the law.
points.apply: Name one grudge and bring it to confession this Lent.

q: Whoever is kind to the poor lends to the LORD, and will be repaid in full.
And the king will answer them, ‘Truly I tell you, just as you did it to one of the least of these who are members of my family, you did it to me.’
points.apply: Do one corporal work of mercy before Sunday.

concl: Holiness is love made concrete in honest hands and a forgiving heart.
On the last day our love will be read in the language of mercy.
2027-02-15.resolve: Choose one work of mercy to practise every week of Lent.

intro: Theme: “It shall not return to me empty.”
The fruitful Word, the trusting prayer of children, and the forgiveness that the Our Father requires.

points.h: Rain that does not return empty
sub: Seed for the sower, bread for the eater.
q: so shall my word be that goes out from my mouth; it shall not return to me empty, but it shall accomplish that which I purpose, and succeed in the thing for which I sent it.

Indeed, the word of God is living and active, sharper than any two-edged sword, piercing until it divides soul from spirit, joints from marrow; it is able to judge the thoughts and intentions of the heart.
points.apply: Read the day's Gospel every morning of Lent.

q: Never be rash with your mouth, nor let your heart be quick to utter a word before God, for God is in heaven, and you upon earth; therefore let your words be few.
Do not be like them, for your Father knows what you need before you ask him.
points.apply: Spend five minutes of prayer today in silent trust.

q: Forgive your neighbor the wrong he has done, and then your sins will be pardoned when you pray.
For if you forgive others their trespasses, your heavenly Father will also forgive you;
points.apply: Forgive one person by name before you pray tonight.

concl: God's Word never falls in vain.
The prayer Jesus taught makes us children who forgive.
2027-02-16.resolve: Pray the Our Father slowly each night this week as a family.

intro: Theme: “See, something greater than Jonah is here!”
The God of second chances, a city that repents from top to bottom, and the sign of the risen Christ.

q: Jonah began to go into the city, going a day's walk. And he cried out, “Forty days more, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!”
The Lord is not slow about his promise, as some think of slowness, but is patient with you, not wanting any to perish, but all to come to repentance.
points.apply: Thank God for one second chance he has given you.

sub: Turning hands as well as hearts.
q: The sacrifice acceptable to God is a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise.
Just so, I tell you, there will be more joy in heaven over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous persons who need no repentance.
points.apply: Make a concrete act of restitution for one wrong you have done.

sub: Do not grow deaf to Christ.
q: But the LORD provided a large fish to swallow up Jonah; and Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights.
The people of Nineveh will rise up at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonah, and see, something greater than Jonah is here!
points.apply: Go to confession before the end of February.

concl: God gives second chances to cities and to sinners.
The risen Christ is the sign: let us turn to him.
2027-02-17.resolve: Celebrate the sacrament of Penance this Lent, and bring your family with you.

intro: Theme: “Ask, and it will be given you.”
Esther's lonely prayer, the persistence Jesus asks of us, and the Golden Rule.

q: On the day I called, you answered me, you increased my strength of soul.
Let us therefore approach the throne of grace with boldness, so that we may receive mercy and find grace to help in time of need.
points.apply: Bring your greatest fear to God in prayer today, in your own words.

q: When you search for me, you will find me; if you seek me with all your heart,
“Ask, and it will be given you; search, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened for you.
points.apply: Keep praying for one intention every day until Easter.

q: And what you hate, do not do to anyone.
“In everything do to others as you would have them do to you; for this is the law and the prophets.
points.apply: Do for someone today what you would want done for you.

concl: God is a Father who loves to give.
The one who receives learns to give.
2027-02-18.resolve: Choose one intention to pray for daily this Lent, and one person to serve.

intro: Theme: “First be reconciled to your brother or sister.”
The God who wants us to live, the root of anger, and the gift that waits for peace.

q: Have I any pleasure in the death of the wicked, says the Lord GOD, and not rather that they should turn from their ways and live?
This is right and is acceptable in the sight of God our Savior, who desires everyone to be saved and to come to the knowledge of the truth.
points.apply: Pray today for someone you have written off as unable to change.

q: He has told you, O mortal, what is good; and what does the LORD require of you but to do justice, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with your God?
For I tell you, unless your righteousness exceeds that of the scribes and Pharisees, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
points.apply: Refuse every insult, even in thought, for one whole day.

q: But there is forgiveness with you, so that you may be revered.
leave your gift there before the altar and go; first be reconciled to your brother or sister, and then come and offer your gift.
points.apply: Visit, call or write to someone with whom you need to be reconciled before Sunday Mass.

concl: No one is beyond the call to turn and live.
God waits for our gift until our hearts are at peace.
2027-02-19.resolve: Before Easter, go first to one person with whom you are not at peace.

intro: Theme: “Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you.”
God's treasured people, a love as wide as the sunrise, and the perfection of the Father.

q: Today the LORD has obtained your agreement: to be his treasured people, as he promised you, and to keep his commandments;
But you are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, God's own people, in order that you may proclaim the mighty acts of him who called you out of darkness into his marvelous light.
points.apply: Renew your baptismal promises in prayer tonight.

sub: Not only those who love us.
q: If your enemies are hungry, give them bread to eat; and if they are thirsty, give them water to drink;
But I say to you, Love your enemies and pray for those who persecute you,
points.apply: Do one kind act for someone who has opposed you.

q: Happy are those whose way is blameless, who walk in the law of the LORD.
Be perfect, therefore, as your heavenly Father is perfect.
points.apply: Ask God each morning of Lent to widen your love by one person.

concl: We are God's treasured people by covenant.
Our love becomes perfect when, like the Father's, it excludes no one.
2027-02-20.resolve: Pray every day of Lent for one person who has hurt you.

intro: Theme: “You are Peter, and on this rock I will build my church.”
The question of Jesus, the rock made by grace, the keys of service and shepherds after the heart of Christ.

points.h: Who do you say that I am?
q: The LORD is my shepherd, I shall not want.
He said to them, “But who do you say that I am?” Simon Peter answered, “You are the Messiah, the Son of the living God.”
points.apply: Write down in one sentence who Jesus is for you, and pray it each morning this week.

sub: The rock and the gates of Hades.
Firm because Christ prayed for him.
q: I will place on his shoulder the key of the house of David; he shall open, and no one shall shut; he shall shut, and no one shall open.
but I have prayed for you that your own faith may not fail; and you, when once you have turned back, strengthen your brothers.”
points.apply: Pray daily this week for the Holy Father, that his faith may not fail.

q: For thus says the Lord GOD: I myself will search for my sheep, and will seek them out.
I will give you the keys of the kingdom of heaven, and whatever you bind on earth will be bound in heaven, and whatever you loose on earth will be loosed in heaven.”
points.apply: Use the keys Christ gave his Church: make a good confession this Lent.
